items.title: NAF airstrike kills ISWAP leaders in Lake Chad
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Precision strikes by the Nigerian Air Force (NAF), operating under Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), have neutralised scores of ISWAP terrorists in the Lake Chad region following the interdiction of an identified terrorist hideout on Monday. Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, Director of NAF Public Relations, said the operation underscores the NAF’s sustained commitment to degrading terrorist networks, disrupting their logistics and enhancing security across Nigeria’s North-East. According to him, “Preliminary post-strike assessments indicate that several prominent Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters were neutralised. “They include individuals identified as key figures within the group’s security structure and leadership Council, like Jindullah, reportedly the Chief Security Guard and confidant of Abu Saleem as well as Abul KissaI, a member of ISWAP Shura Council. “The strike also destroyed logistical assets, including boat engines and motorcycles, believed to support the group’s movement and operational activities. “The operation demonstrates the NAF’s intense effort to conduct intelligence-led precision strikes against terrorist enclaves concealed within difficult terrain. “By neutralising key operatives and destroying critical logistical resources, the strike delivers a significant setback to ISWAP’s operational capability, further constraining its ability to coordinate activities and threaten vulnerable communities. “Commenting on the success, the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, reaffirmed the NAF’s resolve to sustain decisive air operations against terrorist networks in support of ongoing efforts to restore peace and stability across the country. “The Nigerian Air Force remains committed to working closely with sister Services and other security agencies to consolidate operational gains, protect vulnerable communities and advance efforts towards lasting peace and security in the North-East.” The post NAF airstrike kills ISWAP leaders in Lake Chad appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Hadj 2027 : face aux exigences de Riyad, le président Doumbouya préfinance le pèlerinage de 10 000 Guinéens
items.description: Le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, a décidé de préfinancer le pèlerinage à La Mecque de 10 000 fidèles guinéens pour l’édition 2027. Cette mesure intervient alors que l’Arabie saoudite impose aux pays participants des exigences financières strictes, avec un premier versement de plus de 300 milliards de francs guinéens, selon le Secrétariat général des Affaires religieuses. C’est une annonce majeure pour les candidats guinéens au Hadj 2027. Ce lundi 19 octobre 2026, le Secrétariat général des Affaires religieuses (SGAR) a rendu publique la décision du chef de l’État, Mamadi Doumbouya, de préfinancer le pèlerinage de 10 000 fidèles musulmans aux lieux saints de l’islam. Cette initiative vise à permettre à la Guinée de satisfaire aux exigences financières imposées par les autorités saoudiennes et à faciliter la préparation de la prochaine campagne du Hadj. Plus de 300 milliards de francs guinéens mobilisés Selon le Secrétaire général des Affaires religieuses, Karamo Diawara, l’Arabie Saoudite a fixé des conditions financières strictes à l’ensemble des pays participant au pèlerinage de 2027, exigeant notamment un premier versement de plus de 300 milliards de francs guinéens. « L’Arabie saoudite a imposé des exigences financières strictes à l’ensemble des pays participants au Hadj 2027, exigeant un premier versement de plus de 300 milliards de francs guinéens. Grâce à l’intervention du président Mamadi Doumbouya, la Guinée a pu franchir ce cap avec succès », a-t-il expliqué. L’intervention du chef de l’État permet ainsi à la Guinée de franchir cette étape financière déterminante dans la préparation du pèlerinage de 2027. Cette décision intervient alors que les tarifs du Hadj 2027 viennent d’être officiellement fixés. Elle devrait contribuer à faciliter la participation des fidèles concernés et à renforcer les dispositions financières et logistiques nécessaires à l’organisation du pèlerinage. Le Secrétariat général des Affaires Religieuses devrait communiquer ultérieurement les critères d’éligibilité ainsi que les modalités pratiques d’accès à ce dispositif de préfinancement. En attendant ces précisions, les candidats au Hadj sont appelés à suivre les communications officielles des autorités religieuses pour connaître les conditions de participation à cette mesure.

‘I’m very proud of you’ — Tinubu showers praise on CityBoy Movement
items.description: By Bayo Wahab President Bola Tinubu on Tuesday praised the City Boy Movement for what he described as a new model of political organisation in Nigeria, telling its members he was “very proud” of them. The President spoke at the State House during a ceremonial meeting with the group and the Relax Tinubu is Fixing Nigeria (RTIFN) support group. Addressing members of the movement, Tinubu said the group had introduced something new to the country’s politics by going beyond mobilising crowds. “The CityBoy Movement, to all of you, you have done something new in Nigeria politics. You did not just gather people; you built a structure, millions of real, verifiable members,” the President said. He highlighted the group’s national spread, noting that it has “a presence in every state, every local government, every ward, down to the polling units.” The President also commended the movement’s engagement with young people, citing its call centre and its community outreach programme, CityBoy Care. “You drilled down; a call center that speaks to young Nigerians every day and listen to whatever their community needs. CityBoy Care, meeting members where they live,” he said. Tinubu described the group’s approach as organised and purposeful, rather than the product of mere publicity. “That is not noise. That is organisation. That is excellent thinking. That is the kind of seriousness this country needs from its young people, and I’m very proud of you. I must say so,” he said. The President also thanked members for defending his administration publicly, including at moments when doing so carried a political cost. “You were patient when patience was hard. You defended this administration in the market, on the campuses, at the motorparks and on social media even when it was not popular to do so,” Tinubu said. He added that their loyalty had not gone unnoticed. “I saw it, I noticed, and I will never forget it. I say thank you once again,” the President said. The City Boy Movement was founded by the President’s son, Seyi Tinubu, who is also its patron. The post ‘I’m very proud of you’ — Tinubu showers praise on CityBoy Movement appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Where is the 24-hour economy? – Bawumia challenges Mahama government to show results
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has been tearing into the government’s flagship 24-hour economy, delivering a brutal verdict nearly two hours into the NDC administration. Dr Bawumia has challenged the Mahama government to demonstrate progress on its flagship 24-hour economy policy, questioning whether the initiative has delivered the jobs and employment opportunities promised to Ghanaians. Speaking at the NPP’s Thanksgiving service in Sunyani, Dr Bawumia criticised the government’s handling of the policy, arguing that Ghanaians were yet to see tangible results. “We have waited for 2 years, but we cannot see the 24-hour economy. They were just campaign propaganda. They don’t understand for them to come and explain it to us. They themselves don’t understand it. Where is the 24-hour economy?” he asked. He argued that the policy risked remaining an election promise if the government could not translate its commitments into concrete employment opportunities and benefits for the public. Dr Bawumia also challenged the government’s economic recovery narrative, saying improvements in headline indicators such as inflation and the exchange rate would mean little if households continued to struggle financially. “The government says inflation is down, and the dollar is down, but Ghanaians are interested in the pocket economy. They know the pocket economy,” he said. He maintained that economic stability should be reflected in improved living conditions and relief from the financial pressures facing ordinary Ghanaians. “I am saying stability of the economy is meaningless if it cannot be linked up with the total liberation of the suffering of our people,” he added. The former Vice President’s comments form part of the NPP’s criticism of the government’s economic management and its implementation of campaign promises, particularly the 24-hour economy initiative. The policy is a flagship programme of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), aimed at expanding economic activity and creating employment through round-the-clock production and service delivery.

items.title: Après plusieurs semaines de soins à Istanbul, Marcus retrouve Conakry et rassure sur son état de santé
items.description: Après plusieurs semaines de prise en charge médicale à Istanbul, en Turquie, l’artiste guinéen Abdoul Aziz Bangoura, alias Marcus ou Hugo Le God, membre du groupe Banlieuz’art, a regagné Conakry ce dimanche 18 octobre 2026. À son arrivée, il a donné des nouvelles rassurantes de son état de santé, remercié les autorités guinéennes et exprimé sa reconnaissance envers les nombreuses personnes qui l’ont soutenu durant cette période difficile. L’attente prend fin pour les proches et les admirateurs de Marcus. Parti à l’étranger pour recevoir des soins médicaux après la dégradation de son état de santé, le chanteur poursuivait sa prise en charge à Istanbul depuis septembre dernier. Son retour en Guinée marque une nouvelle étape après plusieurs semaines de soins et des interventions chirurgicales, dont l’amputation de son petit orteil. Accueilli à l’aéroport international Ahmed-Sékou-Touré de Conakry, le membre de Banlieuz’art n’a pas caché son bonheur de retrouver sa famille, son public et son pays. À son arrivée, il a tenu à rassurer ses fans sur son état de santé et à apporter des précisions sur l’amputation de son petit orteil, tout en évoquant les rumeurs qui ont circulé sur les réseaux sociaux. « Mon petit orteil a été amputé, ça s’est déformé à un moment. J’ai vu sur la toile que j’avais eu je ne sais pas quoi. Mais en tout cas, tout va bien, rassurez-vous », a-t-il déclaré. Malgré cette épreuve, l’artiste s’est réjoui de retrouver les siens et de constater une amélioration de son état de santé. « Je suis tellement heureux d’être en Guinée, je suis tellement heureux de retrouver ma famille, de vous retrouver, de retrouver mon pays qui m’a tellement manqué et de retrouver à peu près ma santé aussi, qui était dégradée quand je partais. Donc je suis très heureux d’être là, franchement », a-t-il confié, avant d’exprimer son envie de reprendre le travail. Durant cette période de soins à Istanbul, Marcus affirme avoir bénéficié de l’implication des autorités guinéennes, notamment du président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, qu’il a tenu à remercier publiquement. « Je suis heureux de l’entendre parce que moi, je suis en forme. Et grâce à Dieu, je remercie le Tout-Puissant Allah. Je remercie aussi le président de la République, Monsieur Mamadi Doumbouya, pour toute sa bienveillance. Il a tout mis en place, il a secoué tout le monde pour que je sois bien et je suis bien. On a fait mes opérations, tout a été carré, comme vous le savez », a-t-il déclaré. Au-delà de cette reconnaissance, le chanteur a également salué la solidarité manifestée par les Guinéens pendant son absence. Visiblement touché, Marcus est revenu sur l’émotion ressentie en découvrant l’ampleur de la mobilisation autour de lui. Il affirme avoir été particulièrement surpris par les marques d’affection de personnes qu’il ne connaissait pas personnellement. « J’étais très ému. J’ai coulé des larmes, pour être franc. J’ai coulé des larmes, j’ai vu que tout le monde était avec moi, vous tous. Et même ceux qui ne me connaissaient pas m’ont appelé. Et ça m’a touché, ça m’a beaucoup touché. J’étais très, très, très, très, très ému. Et je remercie toute la Guinée pour les prières. Je vous remercie tous », a-t-il confié. Ces témoignages traduisent l’importance du soutien populaire dont l’artiste a bénéficié pendant sa prise en charge médicale à l’étranger. De retour au pays, il a tenu à adresser ses remerciements à toutes les personnes qui ont prié pour son rétablissement. Marcus a également évoqué l’état de santé de son compagnon de scène, Salamane. Selon les dernières nouvelles qu’il a reçues, ce dernier se porterait mieux. « J’ai pris de ses nouvelles avant-hier. On m’a dit qu’il était en pleine forme », a-t-il indiqué. Après plusieurs semaines de soins à Istanbul, le retour de Marcus à Conakry, le 18 octobre, ouvre ainsi une nouvelle page pour l’artiste. Désormais tourné vers la reprise de ses activités, le membre de Banlieuz’art espère retrouver progressivement son rythme professionnel, tandis que ses fans attendent de le revoir sur scène. items.title: Saudi postpones top investment conference to 2027 after Houthi attacks
items.description: A major Saudi investment conference has been postponed to next year, its chief executive officer said on Monday, as the kingdom comes under repeated attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis. The annual Future Investment Initiative (FII), often dubbed “Davos in the Desert”, was scheduled to take place from October 26-29. For nearly a decade, it has served as a showcase for Saudi Arabia’s efforts to attract global investors, business leaders and heads of state. The postponement deals a blow to the kingdom’s ambitions to draw foreign capital, diversify its oil-reliant economy and push its reform agenda. In a statement posted on X, FII Institute CEO Maha Al Saud said the gathering would instead take place in 2027, saying organisers wanted to ensure the anniversary edition delivered the “full scale” and “extraordinary quality” expected by participants. She said new dates would be announced soon, while current registrations and partnerships would remain valid. Three sources familiar with the matter had earlier told AFP the conference would be postponed. One source said organisers “won’t announce a new date soon” while another questioned who would be willing to “risk flying to Riyadh these days”. The decision comes after Riyadh’s international airport, a repeated target of Houthi attacks, suspended operations earlier this month after 13 people were killed in an October 10 strike, with no clear timeline for when air traffic could resume. It was the deadliest attack on the kingdom in more than a decade. Earlier this month, diplomatic sources said the kingdom was planning to move ahead with the conference, offering on-site and virtual attendance, as well as alternative air and land travel routes. But that plan appears to have been scrapped as Western travel warnings for the region have multiplied and the airport remains shut. “The executives I’ve spoken to are very, very, very hesitant to travel to Riyadh for this month’s conferences,” a consultant who advises Saudi firms told AFP. “Companies won’t put their employees in harm’s way for the sake of an investment conference,” they added. AFP The post Saudi postpones top investment conference to 2027 after Houthi attacks appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: LFR et budget 2027: Ousmane Sonko appelle à préserver les ménages et les dépenses sociales
items.description: La loi de finances rectificative et le projet de loi de finances initiale pour 2027 suscitent des divergences entre le gouvernement et PASTEF, formation majoritaire à l'Assemblée nationale. Lors d’une conférence de presse, le leader du parti Ousmane Sonko a notamment évoqué les subventions aux produits pétroliers, la fiscalité, les dépenses sociales et l’encadrement des fonds spéciaux. Le leader du parti défend des ajustements destinés, selon lui, à concilier redressement des finances publiques et préservation du pouvoir d’achat. Subventions aux hydrocarbures : le débat sur les prix La réduction progressive des subventions aux produits pétroliers constitue l’un des principaux points de désaccord soulevés par Ousmane Sonko. Selon les chiffres qu’il a présentés, l’enveloppe consacrée à ces subventions serait ramenée à 552 milliards de FCFA en 2026, contre 790 milliards initialement attendus, soit une baisse de 237 milliards de FCFA. Pour 2027, elle s’établirait à 479 milliards de FCFA. Sur la base de ces projections, le leader de PASTEF estime que le prix du litre de diesel pourrait passer de 755 à environ 867 FCFA en 2026, puis atteindre 910 FCFA en 2027. Il évoque également un prix de 976 FCFA dans l’hypothèse où les subventions seraient limitées à 1 % du produit intérieur brut. Pour limiter les effets d’une éventuelle hausse des prix sur les ménages et les activités économiques, il propose d’agir simultanément sur les subventions et la fiscalité. Il préconise notamment une baisse de la TVA de 18 % à 15 %, accompagnée d’ajustements de certaines taxes spécifiques et des droits de douane. Selon lui, cette approche permettrait de réduire la charge des subventions pour les finances publiques tout en limitant les répercussions sur les prix à la pompe. Il souligne en particulier le rôle du diesel dans les transports et la production, deux secteurs dont les coûts influencent ceux de nombreux biens et services. Ousmane Sonko s’interroge également sur la capacité des mécanismes de compensation sociale à protéger les ménages les plus vulnérables. Il estime que les bourses de sécurité familiale ne suffiraient pas, à elles seules, à compenser les effets indirects d’une hausse des hydrocarbures et appelle à mieux cibler les mesures d’accompagnement. Le plan DEKKAAL, une alternative à évaluer Le plan de redressement économique et social DEKKAAL constitue un autre volet des réserves exprimées par le leader de PASTEF. Celui-ci affirme avoir pris l’initiative de son élaboration lorsqu’il occupait les fonctions de Premier ministre. Il considère que ce programme peut contribuer à mobiliser des ressources supplémentaires sans faire peser l’essentiel de l’effort sur les ménages. D’après les chiffres qu’il a avancés, le plan aurait généré plus de 312 milliards de FCFA au cours de l’année, malgré des difficultés de mise en œuvre. Il estime que les recettes pourraient atteindre au moins 700 milliards de FCFA par an si l’ensemble des mesures prévues était appliqué. Parmi les leviers cités figurent la fiscalité sur certains produits, les transferts d’argent, les jeux de hasard, les licences d’opérateurs et la régularisation foncière. Ousmane Sonko souhaite que ces différentes sources de recettes soient pleinement évaluées avant d’envisager de nouvelles mesures fiscales. Il demande notamment un bilan détaillé des dispositions déjà adoptées concernant les transferts d’argent, avant toute modification supplémentaire. Cette démarche vise, selon lui, à apprécier leur rendement et leur impact avant de revoir le dispositif. Dépenses sociales et investissement : des arbitrages discutés Les orientations budgétaires suscitent également des interrogations concernant les dépenses sociales et l’investissement public. Ousmane Sonko a fait état de réductions budgétaires touchant notamment les ministères chargés de l’Éducation nationale, de la Famille et de la Solidarité ainsi que de la Formation professionnelle. Il a par ailleurs relevé ce qu’il considère comme un décalage entre l’objectif de relance de l’investissement et la baisse de 555 milliards de FCFA qu’il attribue aux dépenses d’investissement dans le projet de loi de finances rectificative. Sur le plan fiscal, le leader de PASTEF soutient le principe du marquage fiscal, qui peut contribuer à mieux suivre la production de certains biens et à améliorer le recouvrement des impôts. Il souhaite toutefois que les produits concernés soient définis par la loi, plutôt que laissés à la seule appréciation du ministre des Finances par arrêté. Il plaide ainsi pour un encadrement permettant à l’Assemblée nationale d’examiner la liste des produits visés. La question des fonds spéciaux figure également parmi les points soulevés. Ousmane Sonko rappelle que leur encadrement fait partie des engagements de PASTEF et annonce que le groupe parlementaire du parti entend défendre des amendements visant à renforcer leur contrôle. Il conditionne le soutien de son parti aux textes budgétaires à la prise en compte de dispositions relatives à ces fonds. Cette position pourrait peser sur les débats parlementaires consacrés à la loi de finances rectificative et au budget de 2027. Relations avec le FMI : un accord technique encore en attente Abordant les discussions avec le Fonds monétaire international (FMI), Ousmane Sonko a rappelé qu’un accord technique avait été trouvé avec l’institution. Il a toutefois souligné que cet accord demeurait provisoire et devait encore être soumis au conseil d’administration du Fonds pour devenir définitif. Il a plaidé pour la recherche de solutions permettant de réorganiser les échéances de la dette tout en préservant les marges de décision économiques du Sénégal. Il a également exprimé des réserves sur le recours à certains mécanismes internationaux de financement, appelant à une réflexion sur le rôle des institutions monétaires régionales, notamment la Banque centrale des États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (BCEAO) et l’UEMOA. Dans son argumentaire, le leader de PASTEF insiste sur la nécessité de concilier le rétablissement des équilibres budgétaires avec la protection du pouvoir d’achat et le maintien des dépenses sociales. Des discussions parlementaires décisives Malgré ses réserves, Ousmane Sonko affirme que PASTEF reste ouvert au dialogue avec le gouvernement. Le parti entend examiner les textes budgétaires et proposer des amendements, sans exclure un vote défavorable si ses principales demandes ne sont pas prises en compte. Les débats parlementaires devront ainsi permettre de préciser les arbitrages retenus en matière de subventions, de fiscalité, d’investissement et de dépenses sociales. Ils donneront également une indication sur la capacité des différentes parties à rapprocher leurs positions autour de la trajectoire budgétaire du Sénégal pour 2026 et 2027. Cheikh Gora DIOP

items.title: France announces curfews as government grapples with unrest
items.description: France announced partial curfews in Paris and other cities on Monday after weekend demonstrations over soaring prices degenerated into some of the worst street violence in recent years. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu did not rule out imposing a state of emergency after the interior minister said police had “lost control”. Tourists in Paris had a taste of the disruption on Monday when they found the Louvre closed because of a small group of student protesters. Facing accusations that it failed to anticipate and respond to the violence, the government has vowed to re-establish order, while officials scrambled to contain public anger. The unrest , erupting just six months before France elects a successor to President Emmanuel Macron, threatened to continue, with organisers calling for a new round of protests next Saturday. Authorities said partial curfews would be enforced from Monday evening to Tuesday morning in a number of cities including Paris, Lille and Lyon, to protect businesses. In the capital, a curfew was ordered from 11pm (2am PKT), while demonstrations were banned from 8pm. “I’m absolutely determined to restore public order”, Lecornu said. Other European countries have also seen demonstrations over rising prices, with smaller clashes breaking out in Milan and Belgium over the weekend and protests simmering in Spain and Portugal. Some half a million people turned out across France on Saturday to denounce the surging cost of living, a culmination of four weeks of protests that began with students demanding better conditions at high schools. What started as peaceful demonstrations descended into violence in many cities, as masked groups attacked law enforcement, broke into public buildings and set some ablaze, looted shops, and set fire to cars, bicycles and scooters. Listings for ‘stolen goods’ On Monday, France’s digital minister, Anne Le Henanff, urged online resale platforms to remove listings for “stolen items” following Saturday’s looting and summoned representatives of companies including Vinted and eBay. CCTV footage shows a masked group breaking into a jewellery shop in Lyon, France, October 17, 2026, in this screengrab obtained from a handout video. — Reuters After the weekend scenes of chaos, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez offered his resignation, but Macron refused to accept it. More than 2,500 people were arrested and nearly 1,000 members of the security forces injured. Protesters were also hurt, with one demonstrator’s hand blown off by a police crowd-control grenade. Macron acknowledged failures in the government response, which had seen 60,000 law enforcement personnel deployed on Saturday. Nationwide, more than 2,513 people have been taken into police custody since the weekend, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said. He added that 67 had been jailed and “dozens” of criminal cases opened. Darmanin also said authorities would use facial recognition on social media to identify perpetrators. At least 3,000 shops were damaged, with the cost running into hundreds of millions of euros. In an address to the nation on Sunday, Macron slammed the “unbridled” violence. The European Union called the violence “unacceptable” but warned that the right to peaceful protest “must be protected” in France. Germany condemned the violence and updated its travel advice for France, saying “further outbreaks of violence in the coming days cannot be ruled out”. China has warned citizens travelling to France to be aware of risks and take safety precautions, state broadcaster CCTV reported. Louvre blocked In Paris on Monday, a dozen demonstrators blocked the entrance to the Louvre, the most visited museum in the world, while bewildered tourists looked on. “We don’t want to get involved. We want to stand back and get away from them,” Pat Boland, a tourist from Australia, said of the protests. The pensioner, 73, spoke to AFP outside barricades that had been erected at the Louvre, which was closed because a small group of protesters stood by its famed glass pyramid entrance. Protesters and students from art and culture schools block the entrance to the Louvre Museum during a demonstration in support of a high school student movement demanding better school conditions and government action, in Paris, France, October 19, 2026. — Reuters The unrest has flared before presidential elections in April and May that will elect a new French president after a decade of centrist Macron. Marine Le Pen, the far-right presidential candidate , is riding high in the polls. The government has accused ultra-left groups of stoking the violence to boost the chances of the far-left firebrand Jean-Luc Melenchon in the presidential polls. The interior minister and intelligence services were to meet late Monday to discuss the violence. Europe During the weekend, clashes broke out on the sidelines of a cost-of-living demonstration in Milan. “I’m very worried because it’s a new phenomenon, which also originates from an international scenario and therefore feeds itself,” mayor Giuseppe Sala said. In Belgium, police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in Brussels and Liege. In Spain protesters have set up tents in the heart of Madrid to denounce soaring housing costs, with similar encampments going up in neighbouring Portugal’s main cities of Lisbon and Porto.

items.title: Trump to Netanyahu: You’ll have ‘tremendous’ election win
items.description: US President Donald Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday he expected him to win a “tremendous” election victory next week, with the Israeli leader suggesting they may again attack Iran together. A day after Trump publicly endorsed Netanyahu in the close-fought October 27 election, the Israeli premier put out a video of the two right-wing leaders lavishing praise on each other by telephone. “I think you’re going to have a tremendous victory, actually,” Trump can be heard saying, with Netanyahu putting his mobile on speakerphone. “You’re the man I want by my side, Bibi,” Trump said, referring to Netanyahu by his nickname. Netanyahu — while reminding the famously loose-lipped president that they were on an open line — hailed Trump for joining Israel in attacking Iran, a decades-long goal of Israel’s longest-serving prime minister. “Donald, we have a job to finish,” Netanyahu said. “We’ll finish it together. We’ll finish it, and no one else will do it.” Netanyahu did not elaborate but again described Iran’s clerical state, which remains in power nearly eight months after the joint massive attack, as “the greatest danger”. AFP The post Trump to Netanyahu: You’ll have ‘tremendous’ election win appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Boffa : deux enfants tués par la foudre à Colia-Lambanyi
items.description: Un drame a endeuillé la commune rurale de Colia-Lambanyi, où deux enfants âgés de 6 à 8 ans ont perdu la vie après avoir été frappés par la foudre, aux environs de 17 heures, dans le marigot de Fangnékhouré. Le drame plonge leurs familles et toute la communauté dans une profonde tristesse. Selon les informations recueillies sur place, les deux victimes, issues du même père, avaient quitté l’école aux environs de 14 heures. Après leur retour à la maison et leur repas, elles se seraient rendues au marigot de Fangnékhouré pour se laver. Les deux enfants faisaient partie d’un groupe de six enfants présents sur les lieux au moment du drame. C’est aux environs de 17 heures, alors que le ciel s’assombrissait et qu’une pluie semblait imminente, que la foudre aurait frappé. Les deux enfants n’ont malheureusement pas survécu, selon les premières informations recueillies. La tragédie a provoqué une vive émotion au sein des familles des victimes et de la communauté locale. Deux jeunes vies ont ainsi été brutalement interrompues, laissant leurs proches dans une douleur immense. Ce drame rappelle les dangers liés aux orages, particulièrement à proximité des marigots, des cours d’eau et dans les espaces découverts. Dès les premiers signes d’un orage, il est recommandé de s’éloigner des points d’eau et de chercher refuge dans un bâtiment solide. À Colia-Lambanyi, l’émotion reste vive après la mort de ces deux enfants, victimes d’un phénomène naturel aussi soudain que dévastateur.

items.title: Tompolo mourns Uduaghan, hails role in Niger Delta peace
items.description: By Akpokona Omafuaire, Warri Chairman of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has mourned former Delta State Governor Emmanuel Uduaghan, crediting him with contributing to peace in the Niger Delta. Tompolo, in a condolence statement issued by his media consultant, Dr Paul Bebenimibo, on Monday, said Uduaghan played a significant role during the peak of militancy in the oil-producing region. He recalled the former governor’s support for the Presidential Amnesty Programme and the pipeline surveillance arrangement introduced during the administrations of late President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua and former President Goodluck Jonathan. The statement said Tompolo received news of Uduaghan’s death with sadness, adding that he did not expect the announcement at this time. It read, “Tompolo recalled the role of the former governor during the days of militancy in the Niger Delta; how the former governor supported the Presidential Amnesty Programme and the pipeline surveillance job awarded during the time of late President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua and former President Goodluck Jonathan.” The Tantita chairman described Uduaghan’s death as a great loss and said the former governor would be greatly missed. He also prayed to God to give the deceased’s family and other mourners the strength to bear the loss. The post Tompolo mourns Uduaghan, hails role in Niger Delta peace appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: DPM Dar arrives in Tajikistan for high-level SCO moot
items.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar arrived in Tajikistan’s capital Dushanbe on Monday to lead Pakistan’s delegation at a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting. Upon arrival, he was received by Tajikistan’s Minister of Energy and Water Resources Daler Juma, Pakistan’s Ambassador to Tajikistan Irfan Ahmed and Pakistan’s national coordinator for the SCO, Khalil Hashmi, along with senior Tajik government officials. Later, he held a meeting with Tajik Prime Minister Qohir Rasulzoda and thanked him for the warm hospitality extended to the Pakistani delegation and appreciated the arrangements for the SCO meeting. According to the Foreign Office (FO), he also congratulated Tajikistan on the 35th anniversary of its independence. “The two leaders reviewed bilateral relations and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation in trade, investment, energy, connectivity, defence and culture, as well as promoting people-to-people exchanges. They also underscored the importance of cooperation on climate change and water security,” it said. “Highlighting Pakistan’s expertise in disaster management, Dar underscored the potential for cooperation with Tajikistan through the National Disaster Management Authority. They also exchanged views on regional developments. Dar reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to working closely with Tajikistan to promote regional peace and deeper economic integration,” it said. DPM Dar also met the first deputy prime minister of Mongolia, Jadambyn Enkhbayar, on the margins of a reception hosted by Rasulzoda for heads of delegations attending the SCO meeting. In addition, he held an informal meeting with the Chinese Prime Minister Li Qiang on the sidelines of the banquet dinner, according to the FO. “The two leaders had a cordial exchange of views on Pakistan-China All Weather strategic relations and current regional developments,” the FO said. Dar is visiting Dushanbe at the invitation of Rasulzoda to attend the SCO’s Council of Heads of Government (CHG) meeting being held from Oct 19-20, according to the FO. The CHG is the SCO’s second-highest decision-making body and provides guidance on economic, financial, trade, connectivity and socio-economic cooperation, as well as the organisation’s budgetary matters, FO noted. “The prime ministers of Belarus, China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan, Iran’s vice president and India’s external affairs minister will also represent their respective countries at the meeting.” During his visit, Dar will also call on Tajikistan’s president and prime minister and hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from SCO member states on the sidelines of the meeting, the FO added. Pakistan assumed the chairmanship of the SCO Council of Heads of State (CHS) for 2027 during an annual summit held in Kyrgyzstan in September. On Oct 1, Dar chaired a follow-up meeting to review preparations for the SCO CHS summit, which Islamabad is scheduled to host in 2027. In July, Pakistan hosted the 12th meeting of the Heads of Border Services of the Competent Authorities of the SCO. Islamabad also chairs SCO’s Reg­ional Anti-Terrorist Structure (SCO-RATS), a role it assumed last September. The country last hosted the SCO CHG meeting in Islamabad in October 2024.

items.title: Banque : Moumounou Gnankambary nommé directeur général de Vista Bank Burkina Faso
items.description: Selon une information publiée par Financial Afrik, Moumounou Gnankambary a été nommé directeur général de Vista Bank Burkina Faso à l'issue d'un conseil d'administration extraordinaire tenu le vendredi 16 octobre 2026 à Bangkok, en Thaïlande. Il succède à Mohamed Ba et aura notamment la responsabilité de conduire le processus de fusion avec Société Générale Burkina Faso. Ancien directeur général du Trésor et de la comptabilité publique, ce haut cadre burkinabè possède une longue expérience de la gestion des finances publiques, de la gouvernance bancaire et des institutions financières régionales et internationales. La nomination de Moumounou Gnankambary à la tête de Vista Bank Burkina Faso intervient à un moment important de l'évolution de cet établissement bancaire. Selon Financial Afrik, la décision a été validée le 16 octobre 2026, lors d'une réunion extraordinaire du conseil d'administration organisée à Bangkok. Le nouveau directeur général prend ainsi les commandes de la banque avec, parmi ses principales missions annoncées, le pilotage du rapprochement avec Société Générale Burkina Faso. Au-delà de ce chantier, sa nomination marque l'arrivée à la direction exécutive de Vista Bank Burkina d'un profil particulièrement expérimenté dans les finances publiques et la gouvernance des institutions financières. Un parcours construit au sommet de l'administration financière burkinabè Né le 28 décembre 1966 à Ouagadougou, Moumounou Gnankambary est titulaire d'une maîtrise en droit public obtenue en 1991 à l'Université de Ouagadougou. Il a ensuite poursuivi sa formation à l'École nationale des régies financières (ENAREF), où il a obtenu, en 1994, un diplôme d'administrateur des services financiers et un diplôme d'études supérieures spécialisées en finances publiques. En 1996, il complète son parcours académique par une spécialisation en élaboration et exécution du budget de l'État à l'Institut international d'administration publique de Paris. Sa carrière professionnelle débute en septembre 1994 à la Direction générale du budget du ministère chargé des Finances, où il exerce comme chargé d'études jusqu'en janvier 2000. Il rejoint ensuite la Présidence du Faso en qualité de directeur des affaires administratives et financières, poste qu'il occupe de janvier 2000 à janvier 2005. En janvier 2005, il est nommé directeur général du budget. Il exercera cette fonction jusqu'en juillet 2007, avant d'accéder, en août de la même année, au poste de directeur général du Trésor et de la comptabilité publique. Pendant près de huit ans, jusqu'en janvier 2015, Moumounou Gnankambary dirige cette administration stratégique, chargée notamment de la gestion de la trésorerie publique et de la comptabilité de l'État. De 2015 à 2021, il poursuit son parcours comme conseiller technique du ministre de l'Économie, des Finances et du Développement. Une expertise sollicitée à l'international Son expérience dépasse les frontières du Burkina Faso. Entre mai 2021 et avril 2022, il intervient en République démocratique du Congo comme expert technique international en gouvernance financière, déployé par Expertise France auprès du gouvernement congolais. Il revient ensuite au Burkina Faso où il occupe, du 31 août au 30 décembre 2022, les fonctions de directeur exécutif du Bureau national des grands projets du Burkina, à la Présidence du Faso. Depuis avril 2024, il était en position de disponibilité et exerçait comme consultant et associé du cabinet G&T Partners. Ces différentes responsabilités lui ont permis de développer une expertise à la fois administrative, budgétaire et institutionnelle, dans des environnements nationaux et internationaux. Une connaissance approfondie des institutions bancaires et monétaires Le parcours de Moumounou Gnankambary ne se limite pas à la haute administration financière. Il est également marqué par une participation à la gouvernance de plusieurs institutions bancaires, financières et économiques. De 2007 à 2015, parallèlement à ses fonctions de directeur général du Trésor et de la comptabilité publique, il a notamment représenté le Burkina Faso au conseil d'administration de la Banque centrale des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (BCEAO). Durant cette même période, il a siégé à la Commission bancaire de l'Union monétaire ouest-africaine (UMOA), en qualité de représentant de l'État burkinabè. Il a également exercé des fonctions de gouverneur suppléant du Burkina Faso auprès du Fonds monétaire international (FMI) et de la Banque d'investissement et de développement de la CEDEAO (BIDC). Il a, par ailleurs, présidé le conseil de gestion du Fonds burkinabè de développement économique et social (FBDES). Avant cela, il avait déjà siégé au conseil d'administration de la Banque internationale du Burkina (BIB), entre 2005 et 2007, ainsi qu'à celui de la Banque ouest-africaine de développement (BOAD). Ces différentes responsabilités lui ont permis de se familiariser avec les enjeux de réglementation bancaire, de supervision financière, de financement du développement et de gouvernance institutionnelle. Une expérience déjà acquise au sein du groupe Vista L'arrivée de Moumounou Gnankambary à la direction générale de Vista Bank Burkina ne constitue pas son premier contact avec le groupe bancaire. En effet, il siège depuis décembre 2016 au conseil d'administration de Vista Bank Guinée en qualité d'administrateur indépendant. Plus récemment, en juin 2026, il a intégré le conseil d'administration de Vista Assurances Niger, avant de rejoindre, en août 2026, celui de Vista Bank Tchad, également comme administrateur indépendant. Cette expérience lui confère une connaissance préalable de la gouvernance de plusieurs entités du groupe Vista, un atout potentiel pour ses nouvelles responsabilités opérationnelles au Burkina Faso. Le nouveau directeur général a également exercé des responsabilités dans d'autres secteurs économiques. Il a notamment présidé le conseil d'administration de la Loterie nationale burkinabè (LONAB) de janvier 2020 à avril 2021, puis celui de la société minière SEMAFO Boungou SA d'août 2023 à juillet 2025. Il a aussi représenté le Burkina Faso au sein de plusieurs autres structures, dont African Risk Capacity (ARC), United Bank for Africa (UBA) Burkina et la Société burkinabè de fibres textiles (SOFITEX). Le défi du rapprochement avec Société Générale Burkina Faso La principale mission annoncée du nouveau directeur général concerne le processus de fusion entre Vista Bank Burkina et Société Générale Burkina Faso. Ce chantier représente un enjeu important pour l'évolution de la présence du groupe Vista sur le marché bancaire burkinabè. Dans un secteur soumis aux exigences de la réglementation bancaire régionale, une telle opération implique notamment des questions de gouvernance, d'organisation, de gestion des risques, de ressources humaines et d'intégration des systèmes d'information. Elle pose également des enjeux de continuité et de qualité des services pour les clients des établissements concernés. À fin décembre 2024, la BCEAO recensait 16 banques et quatre établissements financiers à caractère bancaire au Burkina Faso. Vista Bank Burkina et Société Générale Burkina Faso figuraient toutes deux parmi les établissements bancaires répertoriés. Pour Moumounou Gnankambary, le défi sera donc de mobiliser son expérience de gestionnaire public, ses connaissances des institutions financières et sa familiarité avec le groupe Vista afin d'accompagner cette transformation. Les modalités précises et le calendrier du processus de fusion restent toutefois à préciser. Un profil à la croisée des finances publiques et de la banque Le nouveau directeur général de Vista Bank Burkina présente ainsi un profil particulier : celui d'un haut fonctionnaire des finances publiques ayant progressivement élargi son expérience à la gouvernance des banques et des entreprises. Son parcours, qui s'étend sur plus de trois décennies, l'a conduit de la Direction générale du budget aux plus hautes responsabilités du Trésor public, avant des missions de conseil et de représentation au sein d'institutions financières nationales et internationales. Il est également titulaire de plusieurs distinctions honorifiques, dont celles de chevalier de l'Ordre national en 2009 et d'officier de l'Ordre national en 2017. Avec sa nomination à Vista Bank Burkina, Moumounou Gnankambary ouvre une nouvelle étape de sa carrière, cette fois à la tête d'un établissement bancaire. Sa capacité à conduire le rapprochement annoncé avec Société Générale Burkina Faso constituera l'un des principaux enjeux de son mandat. Lefaso.net

items.title: Govt slashes petrol price by Rs5.16 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Rs7.69
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · " style="width: 100%; min-height: 50px; max-height: 30000px; border: none; overflow: hidden; display: block;" scrolling="no"> The government on Monday cut the price of petrol by Rs5.16 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs7.69. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs381.14 per litre while HSD will cost Rs389.27 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 20 (Tuesday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Making Ghana’s 5G investment deliver for businesses and the economy
items.description: At a busy shop in Kumasi, a customer waits while an electronic payment stalls. In a diagnostic centre, medical images await transfer to a specialist. A guesthouse loses a booking when its internet connection drops, while an engineering firm waits for a large design file before it can finish a client’s work. For these businesses, connectivity affects income, customer confidence and the time available to serve the next person. Now consider what more dependable connectivity could make possible: a retailer keeping stock records and online orders up to date during the afternoon rush; a student joining a practical lesson remotely without repeated interruptions; a logistics company receiving timely updates to organise deliveries; or a small professional firm serving clients elsewhere in Ghana without travelling for every meeting. These are practical opportunities through which Ghana’s 5G investment could improve everyday services and expand the reach of local businesses. The gains depend on more than speed. A payment terminal needs a connection that remains available. A diagnostic centre needs adequate upload capacity. A hotel needs enough capacity for guests and business systems to work simultaneously. Each needs a service suited to its workload, at a price it can sustain. Spectrum licensing opens the way for operators to provide these services. Turning that opportunity into economic value requires investment in networks, affordable access and businesses equipped to use connectivity effectively. Ghana’s progress should therefore be measured through fewer disrupted transactions, work completed sooner and customers served more reliably. Those outcomes give the country’s 5G investment a purpose that businesses and the public can recognise. From spectrum awards to usable services On 15 July 2026, the National Communications Authority removed the exclusive wholesale 5G rights of Next Gen Infraco Limited, commonly known as NGIC, while preserving the remainder of its licence and spectrum assignment. The amendment opens space for competing deployments while retaining NGIC in the infrastructure landscape. MTN Ghana’s announcement on 2 October reported an award notice for spectrum in the 700 MHz and 3 GHz bands, with fees totalling US$202 million for 15-year licences. At that announcement, payment obligations and formalities were being finalised, with deployment to follow licence issuance. Graphic Online separately reported Telecel’s award of three 2.3 GHz lots, quoting company confirmation. An award, an issued licence and an available retail service are different stages. A business still needs installed infrastructure, compatible equipment and a provider able to activate service at its premises. Public reporting should make these stages clear so that businesses can plan against verified availability. Spectrum fees are one component of operators’ network investment. Radios, transmission infrastructure and power systems require capital expenditure, followed by recurring energy, maintenance and operating costs. Customers face separate calculations: equipment and installation charges they bear, subscription fees and usage charges. Those costs should be assessed against improvements in the customer’s work and earnings. Coverage must translate into working connections Coverage describes where a connection may be obtainable; capacity describes how much traffic a network can carry while users compete for it. Lower-frequency spectrum, such as 700 MHz, helps extend reach and penetrate buildings. Wider mid-band allocations provide room for greater capacity, subject to the bandwidth activated, antenna configuration, interference and user conditions. A business can therefore lie within a coverage area and still experience slow transfers when demand rises. A hotel needs adequate service when guests return in the evening. A commercial district needs capacity when many businesses are trading simultaneously. Installation tests should reflect those conditions and the equipment’s intended location inside the premises. The NCA’s clarified 70 per cent outdoor mobile-broadband population target for March 2027 is technology-neutral. It should not be read as a guarantee of usable 5G at every premises within that population. Coverage figures need to be accompanied by evidence of experienced performance. This matters especially for smaller businesses and communities beyond the largest commercial centres. A connection that is nominally available but unaffordable or unreliable cannot support regular use. Deployment policy should assess both network reach and the practical conditions under which customers can participate. Wireless broadband needs capacity and reliable installation Fixed wireless access connects premises to a cellular network through installed receiving equipment. It can offer an alternative where fibre installation is costly or slow. Fixed customers, however, share radio capacity with mobile users. Ericsson’s planning guidance considers their combined demand during the busiest periods. For illustration, twenty businesses simultaneously requiring 20 megabits per second need 400 megabits per second of useful download capacity before mobile traffic and operating headroom. This is a demand calculation, not a measurement of Ghanaian cell capacity. An advertised “up to 100 Mbps” subscription identifies a maximum speed; it does not establish reserved capacity or minimum performance during congestion. Uploads deserve particular attention. Medical images, engineering files and cloud backups move towards the network. A one-gigabyte file contains approximately 8,000 megabits. At a sustained upload rate of 10 Mbps, its theoretical transfer time is about thirteen minutes; at 50 Mbps, it is under three minutes. Actual transfers take longer when overheads and interruptions are included. Improvement has economic value when it helps complete work sooner or avoids delays elsewhere. Providers should test reception, select suitable indoor or outdoor equipment and check the customer’s local network. Poor office Wi-Fi can restrict performance even when the external connection is adequate. Reliability also depends on power and backhaul, the transmission links connecting radio sites to the wider network. A backup subscription may share the primary connection’s mast, transmission route or power dependency. Resilience arrangements must address those shared points of failure. International lessons for Ghana Kenya demonstrates the importance of entry costs. In October 2023, Safaricom reduced its 5G router price from KES25,000 to KES9,999 while expanding coverage into selected towns across 35 counties. At an indicative exchange rate for the announcement date, those prices were approximately GH¢1,970 and GH¢790. These are historical comparisons, not current Ghanaian equipment prices. The announcement shows an effort to lower the adoption barrier, not proof that cheaper equipment produced business growth. Ghanaian packages should combine affordable equipment with installation qualification and transparent usage terms. Instalments may ease cash flow without reducing total cost; allowances and fair-use restrictions can affect whether a package supports daily work. India offers a model for application testing. Its Ministry of Communications reported 100 5G laboratories in March 2026. Ghanaian universities, operators and businesses could jointly test applications in health, education and logistics against available 4G, fibre or Wi-Fi alternatives. A logistics pilot should measure dispatch delays or completed deliveries, with an operational manager responsible for putting the application into daily use. Laboratory activity alone does not establish commercial success. The United Kingdom illustrates why performance claims need measurement. Ofcom’s Mobile Matters 2025 found standalone 5G’s average response time about 15 per cent lower than non-standalone, but its connection success rate was also lower: 95.9 against 97.6 per cent. Standalone 5G uses a 5G core, the systems managing connections beyond the radio network; non-standalone builds on existing 4G infrastructure. These crowdsourced observations were not a controlled technology comparison or a forecast for Ghana. They demonstrate why buyers need several measures together. Faster responses have limited value when an application cannot establish its connection. Ghana should report performance with clear sampling methods and measurement endpoints. Make investment and accountability practical Businesses should establish the existing connection’s performance before testing a replacement. A 90-day pilot can measure consultation interruptions, completed transfers or productive hours recovered, alongside the full additional cost of equipment, integration and service. Consider a hypothetical business generating GH¢3,000 in additional monthly contribution and removing GH¢1,000 of avoidable costs. Contribution means revenue remaining after the variable costs of earning it. With additional operating costs of GH¢1,500, the net monthly gain is GH¢2,500. An initial outlay of GH¢10,000 would have a simple payback of four months, assuming recurring gains and excluding financing and tax. Saved staff time counts only when productively redeployed or translated into an actual saving. Business associations can aggregate demand from smaller firms, giving providers a clearer basis for installation and capacity planning. Providers should specify minimum performance at qualified premises, restoration targets and remedies for failure. Pilot results should include unsuccessful cases so that investment decisions reflect operating conditions. The NCA should publish clear award and licence status and independently checked deployment milestones. Coverage reporting should be supplemented with working-hour download and upload performance, responsiveness and availability. Infrastructure-sharing and wholesale access arrangements should also be monitored as competition develops. Ghana’s service economy will gain when better connectivity enables businesses to serve customers reliably and complete more valuable work. That requires suitable networks, commercially sustainable packages and users equipped to benefit. These outcomes should guide the country’s assessment of its 5G investment. The author, Prof. Abdul-Rahman Ahmed, is Head of the Department of Telecommunication Engineering at KNUST and founder of Stratfound Consult.

items.title: Nico Williams’ agent finally explains failed Barcelona move in 2025
items.description: Barcelona’s inability to provide guarantees over Nico Williams’ registration derailed the proposed move in the summer of 2025, his agent, Félix Tainta, has finally revealed. The Spanish football powerhouse had been keen to sign the Spain international, with their interest extending over two summers, following his top-class performances for both Spain and Athletic Bilbao. Williams became one of the most sought-after players in Europe in summer 2024 after playing an integral role in Spain’s success at the 2024 European Championship and helping Athletic Bilbao end their 40-year trophy drought by winning the Copa del Rey. According to Tainta, negotiations had taken place between Barcelona and Bilbao over a possible transfer of the enterprising attacker. However, the move ultimately fell through over Barcelona’s inability to guarantee Williams’ registration under La Liga’s financial regulations. “We were in talks with Barcelona and Athletic Bilbao were aware of this. They knew what was happening throughout the process, although the club was not happy with Barcelona’s actions,” he said, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo. “As the negotiations progressed, it became clear that Nico Williams could not afford to take the risk of not playing. It’s like a Formula 1 car; if I move into your house, I shouldn’t inherit your problems. I made that perfectly clear to Barcelona,” he added. “We decided, in the absence of specific guarantees, that we could not risk Nico going there and then ending up without playing. He is a professional and needs to practice his profession, especially with the World Cup approaching at that time,” he explained. “If I come to your house to do my job, I should be able to continue doing it and your problems shouldn’t affect me. If you can’t ensure that doesn’t happen, maybe I should change my mind. That’s exactly what happened,” Tainta concluded. Williams ultimately remained at Athletic Bilbao, where he has established himself as one of the club’s most important attacking players.

items.title: Dangote accepts Bae U Barbie’s invitation to appear on YouTube show
items.description: Africa’s richest man, Aliko Dangote, has agreed to appear on Nigerian content creator Bae U Barbie’s YouTube programme, Curiosity Made Me Ask, following an invitation to engage younger audiences. Bae U Barbie, born Adebayo Ridwan, extended the invitation while questioning the billionaire about his media engagements and the need to reach young Nigerians interested in his business and its planned initial public offering (IPO). The content creator observed that most of Dangote’s interviews had been conducted on platforms that were not popular among younger audiences, despite their interest in investing in his company. “Most of the interviews we’ve seen you have been on platforms that my generation don’t watch,” Bae U Barbie said in a video posted on social media on Monday. He clarified that he was not asking Dangote to dismiss his media team but urged the businessman to consider appearing on his show after completing his existing engagements. “I’m not saying you should sack your media team. No, but you know, when you finish,” he said before asking when the billionaire would feature on the programme. Responding, Dangote acknowledged the importance of engaging younger Nigerians, describing them as the country’s future while admitting that his generation had not done enough for Nigeria and Africa. “Honestly, the future that we have is actually you, the youth. We, our own generation, really, we have not really done very well for Nigeria and also for Africa. That’s the truth,” he said. The billionaire stressed the need for older Nigerians to share their experiences with younger people to help them understand the country’s history and development. “So we need to sit down with some of you and discuss our own experience with you,” he added. Dangote also observed that many young Nigerians were unfamiliar with some prominent figures and events from the country’s past. He cited former President Olusegun Obasanjo, suggesting that younger people might know more about him because he returned to power. Bae U Barbie interrupted to highlight his own contribution to making Obasanjo accessible to younger audiences, saying, “Thanks to me. I gave him the platform, sir,” apparently referring to his interview with the former president. Agreeing that younger audiences deserved more of his attention, Dangote said he would be willing to engage them through platforms such as Bae U’s show. “So really, you are right. Going forward, this sort of audience is the audience that we, somebody like me, should actually face,” he said. The businessman also praised the support and respect he receives from young people, including during his trips abroad. He recalled that people accompanying him sometimes attempted to stop members of the public from taking photographs with him. However, he said he preferred to oblige those who approached him. Dangote traced the gesture to an experience from his younger years, when he and his grandfather met prominent personalities in Washington and requested photographs with them. He said the memory had shaped his attitude towards people seeking pictures with him, despite his status as a billionaire. The industrialist also dismissed interpretations of a photograph he shared on social media, explaining that his remarks about divine blessings were not a request for more. “I wasn’t begging for anything. What I was saying, I was just saying that, God, you have overblessed me,” he said. Dangote subsequently indicated his willingness to join Bae U Barbie on Curiosity Made Me Ask, where younger Nigerians could ask questions about his business journey and the factors behind his success. “We will come,” he said, accepting the invitation. He added that he wanted the proposed interaction to be an open conversation in which participants could freely ask how he built his business and achieved his current position. items.title: Troops rescue 11 passengers, foil kidnap attempt in Kogi
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the 12 Composite Brigade of the Nigerian Army have foiled a kidnapping attempt and rescued 11 passengers along Kabba-Ayere Road in Kabba/Bunu Local Government Area of Kogi State. The Acting Assistant Director, Army Public Relations, 12 Composite Brigade, Lieutenant Hassan Abdullahi, disclosed this in a statement, saying the incident occurred on October 18, 2026. He said troops deployed at the patrol base in Kabba were on routine patrol when they responded to credible intelligence about suspected terrorists attempting to abduct passengers travelling in a commercial vehicle along the route. “On arrival, the troops made contact with the terrorists and engaged them, forcing them to abandon the victims and flee into the surrounding bush,” he said. Abdullahi said nine passengers, including the driver, were rescued during the initial operation. He added that the driver and two other passengers who sustained injuries were evacuated for medical attention, while the commercial vehicle was handed over to the appropriate authorities. According to him, troops conducted a follow-up operation on October 19, 2026, during which they searched the area and rescued two additional passengers who had fled into the bush during the encounter. The operation brought the total number of rescued passengers to 11. Abdullahi said the operation underscored the brigade’s commitment to protecting lives and property, denying terrorists freedom of action and improving the safety of commuters across Kogi State. He urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing operations. The Nigerian Army, he added, remained committed to sustaining efforts to safeguard lives and property and ensure the security of residents of Kogi State. items.title: AbdulRazaq inaugurates Tinubu door-to-door campaign in Kwara
items.description: …Tasks APC members on issue-based engagement …Tompolo donates 34 campaign vehicles to movement By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq on Monday inaugurated the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu (PBAT) Door-to-Door Movement in Ilorin, as the group began mobilising support for the President’s re-election in 2027. At the inauguration of the movement’s executives, AbdulRazaq urged members to intensify grassroots mobilisation and communicate the impact of Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda to residents across the state. He commended the movement’s leadership for establishing a platform to communicate the Federal Government’s policies and programmes to the people. The governor charged members to listen to residents’ concerns, provide feedback to the government and explain its programmes effectively. He also urged them to obtain accurate information about government initiatives through official channels and share it with residents, while emphasising the need for peaceful and respectful engagement. “The movement must not only take government messages to the people but also bring their concerns back to the relevant authorities to guide policy adjustments and improve living standards,” AbdulRazaq said, warning members against violence during their engagements. He called for cooperation between the movement and all All Progressives Congress (APC) structures, from the national leadership to ward officials and polling unit committees, saying they were working towards a common goal. The governor added that the initiative should be sustained beyond the inauguration, with activities translating into continuous grassroots engagement rather than a one-off event. The Speaker of the Kwara State House of Assembly and APC governorship candidate, Rt. Hon. Salihu Yakubu Danladi, said he expected residents to vote massively for the party, citing what he described as AbdulRazaq’s achievements across the state’s 193 wards. Danladi said the governor had performed well in infrastructure, civil service reforms, pension administration and the welfare of youths, women and senior citizens. He said the APC had sufficient achievements to campaign on and did not need to resort to insults against political opponents. Danladi urged the movement to remain focused on mobilising support for the party, expressing confidence that the APC would secure substantial votes in Kwara in 2027. “Tinubu is for Kwara, and Kwara is for Tinubu. By God’s grace, 2027 is for the APC. We know where we are today, and we are moving forward,” he said. The state APC Chairman, Prince Sunday Fagbemi, also expressed confidence in the party’s prospects ahead of the 2027 general elections, saying it was determined to win all elective positions in the state. Fagbemi said the party was committed to securing victory for Tinubu, its governorship candidate and candidates contesting National and State Assembly seats. He dismissed claims of alternative political arrangements in Kwara, saying statements by Tinubu and the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory had reinforced the party’s position. He also warned opposition groups against relying on financial inducements to challenge the APC. The founder and grand patron of the movement, High Chief Government Oweizide Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, urged residents to support Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections. Represented by High Chief Kestin Pondi, Ekpemupolo said electing APC candidates at all levels of government would strengthen the President’s ability to implement policies aimed at stabilising the economy and promoting national development. He urged Nigerians not to be misled by political opponents, arguing that continued support for Tinubu would help improve security, infrastructure, healthcare and education. Ekpemupolo also announced the donation of 34 campaign vehicles to the movement to support its grassroots mobilisation activities across Kwara. The National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Comrade Sunday Adekanbi Asuku, urged residents to support Tinubu in the forthcoming election. Asuku commended AbdulRazaq’s record in the state and his support for the President, saying the governor’s achievements had been aided by the Federal Government’s backing. Highlighting Tinubu’s record, the national coordinator said the Federal Government had continued to promote industrial harmony, citing what he described as the absence of prolonged strikes by the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU). The post AbdulRazaq inaugurates Tinubu door-to-door campaign in Kwara appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘It’s easier you put me in prison than take my phone away’ — Dangote
items.description: Africa’s richest man, Aliko Dangote has said he would rather be imprisoned than have his phone taken away, describing losing access to the device as a “no-go area”. Dangote made the remark at an event in Lagos where he unveiled his “Vision 2030” plan for Africa’s industrial revolution. During the event, the billionaire businessman was asked to choose between spending one week without his phone or giving up access to his private jet. Responding to the question, Dangote said he would find it more difficult to part with his phone than his private jet. “Ah… I think it’s easier you put me in prison than to take my phone away. So, you know, I mean taking my phone away is no-go area, okay?” The industrialist also revealed that he has more than 13,000 contacts saved on his phone, highlighting the importance of the device in maintaining his extensive network of personal and professional relationships. “I know that would be almost… my number — I have that number since… Twitter… I have more than 13,000 contacts on my phone.” Reacting to the size of his contact list, Dangote added that he rarely blocks people, suggesting that this has contributed to the large number of contacts on his device. “Wow. Wow. I hardly… I don’t like blocking people, so a lot of people” His comments offer a glimpse into how the billionaire uses his phone to maintain connections, even as he oversees business interests spanning manufacturing, cement, fertiliser, oil refining and other sectors across Africa. Dangote is the president and chief executive of Dangote Group, one of Africa’s largest industrial conglomerates. Vanguard News The post ‘It’s easier you put me in prison than take my phone away’ — Dangote appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Emploi et protection sociale : le gouvernement annonce des recrutements et des régularisations
items.description: Le gouvernement met en avant plusieurs mesures en faveur de l’emploi public, de la régularisation des travailleurs et de l’élargissement de la couverture sociale. Selon le ministre de la Fonction publique, du Travail et de la Réforme du Service public, Mamadou Lamine DIANTE, 4 527 recrutements d’enseignants ont été engagés, tandis que 2 500 agents de santé sont en cours de recrutement. Le renforcement des effectifs dans les secteurs de l’éducation et de la santé figure parmi les mesures présentées par le gouvernement dans le cadre du suivi du pacte de stabilité sociale. Lors du point de presse gouvernemental du lundi 19 octobre 2026, Mamadou Lamine DIANTE a fait état de 4 527 recrutements d’enseignants engagés, dont 2 000 déjà effectués et 2 527 en cours. À ces effectifs s’ajoutent 500 enseignants-chercheurs recrutés et 2 500 agents de santé dont le recrutement est en cours. Ces opérations doivent contribuer au renforcement des ressources humaines dans les services publics. Le ministre a également évoqué les efforts de régularisation des situations administratives. Dans son département, deux guichets uniques ont permis de produire 2 157 actes administratifs concernant plus de 2 500 agents. La plupart des agents concernés ont été mis en solde, selon ses déclarations. La situation des travailleurs licenciés dans certaines entreprises publiques et structures parapubliques a également été abordée. À Dakar Dem Dikk, le gouvernement fait état de la conversion de 214 contrats de prestation en contrats à durée indéterminée (CDI). Mamadou Lamine DIANTE a par ailleurs indiqué que huit travailleurs licenciés avaient été réintégrés, les autres situations évoquées étant notamment liées, selon lui, à des abandons de poste. Au Port autonome de Dakar, 85 réintégrations avaient déjà été effectuées. La régularisation de 162 autres agents est engagée depuis le 12 octobre. Le gouvernement entend notamment convertir en CDI les contrats de travailleurs ayant cumulé plus de deux contrats à durée déterminée. Au ministère des Mines, 44 licenciements restent en cours de traitement. Deux issues sont envisagées : la réintégration des travailleurs concernés ou la conclusion d’un pacte social avec ceux qui ne pourraient pas être réintégrés. Vers un élargissement de la couverture sociale Sur le volet de la protection sociale, le gouvernement cite la mise en place de l’institution de prévoyance maladie des travailleurs non permanents et le déploiement de la Mutuelle sociale nationale des artisans du Sénégal. L’entrée en vigueur du nouveau Code de la sécurité sociale doit également contribuer à étendre la couverture aux travailleurs jusque-là exclus, notamment les indépendants et les acteurs de l’économie informelle. Le gouvernement présente ces mesures comme des avancées vers une couverture sociale plus inclusive. Leur mise en œuvre reste toutefois liée à plusieurs contraintes, notamment les ressources financières disponibles et les études techniques nécessaires à certaines réformes. Ces dossiers figurent parmi les engagements suivis dans le cadre du pacte de stabilité sociale, dont les autorités souhaitent améliorer le taux d’exécution au cours des prochains mois. Cheikh Tidiane NDIAYE
