items.title: Décès de Sidya Touré – Amara Camara appelle à la retenue : « nous ne voulons pas que ces sujets continuent à être entretenus »
items.description: Le ministre secrétaire général de la Présidence de la République et porte-parole de la Présidence, le général Amara Camara, a appelé ce lundi 19 octobre 2026 à mettre fin aux controverses autour du décès de l’ancien Premier ministre Sidya Touré. Il invite les Guinéens à privilégier les prières pour le repos de son âme et le respect de sa mémoire. Lors d’une conférence de presse du porte-parolat du gouvernement, organisée à la Camayenne, à Conakry, le général Amara Camara s’est exprimé sur la disparition de Sidya Touré, décédé le 25 septembre dernier à Paris. La rencontre s’est tenue en présence de Faya François Bourouno, ministre de la Modernisation de l’Administration et de la Fonction publique et porte-parole du gouvernement, ainsi que d’Elhadj Thierno Mamadou Bah, porte-parole adjoint de la Présidence de la République. Rappelant le parcours de l’ancien chef du gouvernement, le porte-parole de la Présidence a déclaré : « On vient de parler du stage d’encadrement. Un autre point par rapport à l’introduction était l’hommage au premier ministre Sidya Touré. Le 25 septembre dernier à Paris, le premier ministre Sidya Touré a été rappelé à Dieu. Le premier ministre Sidya Touré fut premier ministre de 1996 à 1999. Il fut également député de la République », a-t-il indiqué. Face aux nombreuses réactions et aux débats suscités par la disparition de l’ancien responsable politique, le général Amara Camara a exprimé le souhait de voir ces discussions prendre fin. « Il y a eu beaucoup de sujets par rapport à son décès. Nous souhaiterions ici dire que le premier ministre Sidya est décédé. Pour le respect, pour sa mémoire, pour le respect pour son âme, nous ne voulons pas que ces sujets continuent à être entretenus », a-t-il insisté. Pour lui, l’heure est désormais au recueillement. « Ce que nous demandons à chacun, c’est de prier pour le repos de son âme. Il a servi ce pays, il a servi ce pays, il a aimé ce pays », a poursuivi le ministre secrétaire général de la Présidence. Le général Amara Camara a également invoqué les valeurs religieuses pour appeler au respect de la mémoire du défunt. « Une de nos religions nous recommande de ne dire que du bien de ceux qui sont partis. Il fut un monsieur bien, paix à son âme », a-t-il conclu. Par cette déclaration, le porte-parole de la Présidence appelle ainsi à l’apaisement autour du décès de Sidya Touré, invitant les Guinéens à privilégier les prières et le respect de la mémoire de celui qui a dirigé le gouvernement guinéen de 1996 à 1999. Mayi Cissé L’article Décès de Sidya Touré – Amara Camara appelle à la retenue : « nous ne voulons pas que ces sujets continuent à être entretenus » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Education Minister refers Obuasi SHS headmaster’s sexual misconduct allegations to CID
items.description: The Minister for Education, Haruna Iddrisu, has referred allegations of sexual misconduct involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Zakaria Abdulai, and female students to the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) for investigation. The move is intended to allow the police to investigate the criminal aspects of the allegations while education authorities conduct separate administrative inquiries. Speaking to Accra-based Citi News, Mr Iddrisu confirmed that the headmaster had been interdicted pending investigations, stressing that the government would not tolerate sexual misconduct in schools. “Any act of sexual misconduct involving a teacher and a student amounts to abuse of office, and government takes strong exception to it. We have forwarded it to the criminal investigation department to deal with the criminal aspects of it whilst I’ve asked for the suspension of the headmaster without prejudice whilst we look into the merits of the case,” he said on Monday, October 19. Mr Iddrisu also disclosed that the government was considering broader measures to address indiscipline in schools, including the introduction of stronger regulations to guide the conduct of students and teachers. He said a committee would soon be established to advise the government on the matter. The Minister further indicated his support for making the Ghana Education Service’s (GES) code of conduct and standards legally binding under Article 11 of the 1992 Constitution. The GES announced Mr Abdulai’s interdiction in a statement issued on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, to facilitate investigations into the allegations. The case reportedly triggered a student rampage at the school, during which some school property was destroyed, forcing the temporary closure of the institution. The allegations remain subject to investigation.

items.title: Reject Tinubu’s second term, petrol discount a scam – ADC campaign to youths
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has urged Nigerian youths to reject President Bola Tinubu’s second-term bid, accusing his administration of failing to address unemployment and economic hardship while faulting its petrol price discount as misleading. The council said young Nigerians continued to face rising living costs and limited job opportunities, urging them to mobilise for an alternative ahead of the presidential election. The Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC-PCC, Kola Ologbondiyan, made the call during an interaction with ADC youth leaders in Kabba/Bunu Local Government Area of Kogi State. Ologbondiyan said many graduates had been pushed into petty trading and point-of-sale businesses by the scarcity of decent jobs. “As youths, you have spent almost 12 years under the APC government confronting difficult economic circumstances, with many graduates struggling to find decent employment,” he said. He also questioned the government’s petrol price discount, saying pump prices remained above ₦1,400 per litre despite the announced reduction to ₦1,350. “Check the filling stations in your neighbourhood, and you will discover that Nigerians are still paying above ₦1,400 per litre. What, then, is the reality behind this so-called discount?” he queried. Ologbondiyan urged youths to support the ADC’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, and his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, claiming their ticket offered a more transparent approach to managing the petroleum sector and tackling economic hardship. “After years in government, Nigerians deserve more than promises, excuses and propaganda. They deserve policies that work and leadership that understands their pain,” he said. He urged young Nigerians to mobilise across their wards, warning that another APC term would leave their concerns unresolved. “Your future is too important to be sacrificed on the altar of political propaganda. Nigerian youths deserve decent jobs, affordable living conditions and a government that takes their aspirations seriously,” Ologbondiyan said. The post Reject Tinubu’s second term, petrol discount a scam – ADC campaign to youths appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: UMB appoints Justina Stella Laing as COO to advance its brand transformation agenda
items.description: Universal Merchant Bank (UMB) has appointed Justina Stella Laing as Chief Operating Officer (COO). She will lead the operational engine driving UMB’s transformation, leveraging her proven track record of converting ambitious strategies into dependable results. Justina Laing is an accomplished financial services executive with over 18 years of experience leading operations, strategy and large-scale financial initiatives across corporate and investment banking, project and infrastructure finance, syndicated lending and risk management. She has managed complex, multi-billion-dollar portfolios and led financing and fundraising mandates exceeding $2.6 billion, working with governments, central banks, development finance institutions, multinational partners and private-sector clients. She previously held senior roles at CalBank PLC and, more recently, provided financial advisory and consultancy services in the energy and agribusiness sectors. Her career is distinguished by her ability to translate strategy into action. She has played pivotal roles in establishing new business units, fortifying governance and risk frameworks, implementing digital and process improvements, and integrating ESG and sustainability practices into core business operations. For UMB, this appointment underscores a core value of the Bank’s identity: reliability. Reliability is an ongoing commitment delivered through well-executed processes, robust governance, capable personnel and systems that consistently serve customers. It is built into a bank’s operations—precisely where Justina’s experience will be invaluable. Dr. Philip Oti-Mensah, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of UMB, commented on the appointment: “Reliability is not a slogan; it is an operating discipline that must be built, measured, and delivered every single day. “Justina Laing has dedicated her career to transforming ambitious strategies into disciplined results across multi-billion-dollar mandates, new business units, and strengthened governance. “As COO, she completes our leadership team and will ensure UMB delivers on its promises. This is precisely what is required to be Ghana’s most reliable relationship bank.” Turning Strategy into Delivery UMB’s transformation focuses on enhancing customer experience, improving operational efficiency and deepening client relationships. Each of these objectives is ultimately achieved or missed in operations—in how processes function, risks are managed, technology is used, and teams are led. This is the foundation upon which Justina Laing has built her career. Her experience in establishing new business units, strengthening governance and risk frameworks and driving digital and process improvements provides UMB with an operator capable of converting strategic direction into daily, scalable performance. As COO, Justina Laing will oversee the Bank’s operations, technology and process functions, driving efficiency, service quality, governance and risk discipline across the organisation. Beyond her executive career, Justina Laing serves as a Non-Executive Director on several boards, offering strategic perspective and sound governance. She is respected for her integrity, collaborative leadership style and commitment to long-term value creation. She is also passionate about developing people and fostering environments where teams can perform at their best. She holds a master’s degree in Agribusiness from the University of Florida. Commenting on her appointment, Justina Laing stated: “I am delighted to join the UMB team at this exciting stage of the Bank’s journey. “I look forward to working closely with my colleagues across the Bank to deliver excellent customer experiences, strengthen our relationships with customers, and contribute to UMB’s continued growth and success. Together, I believe we can build on the progress already made and take the Bank to the next level.” Since 1972, UMB has built its reputation on supporting its customers and communities when it matters most. With Justina’s appointment, the Bank strengthens this legacy with the operational leadership required to continue delivering on this commitment today and for years to come.

items.title: Última hora del temporal en España, en directo | Se levanta el confinamiento en los ocho municipios de la Comunidad Valenciana
items.description: La Generalitat ha levantado el confinamiento en los ocho municipios de la Comunitat Valenciana donde estaba aún vigente esta medida por la dana, que ha obligado a efectuar más de un millar de rescates este lunes, y se va a desmovilizar a la Unidad Militar de Emergencias (UME) ante la mejora de la situación. Una segunda persona ha fallecido en la localidad valenciana de Oliva tras el paso de la dana Adam , según ha informado un portavoz del Consorcio Provincial de Bomberos de València y han confirmado fuentes gubernamentales. El cadáver de un hombre ha sido hallado en un cámping de la localidad y, según las primeras informaciones, ha fallecido de un infarto. Esta cuarta víctima mortal se suma a los fallecimientos registrados en Barcelona el sábado; en Sagunto el domingo y el de otra persona también en Oliva, este lunes. La fase más adversa de la dana Adam ha azotado con violencia la Comunidad Valenciana durante la madrugada, con lluvias torrenciales de hasta 700 litros por metro cuadrado en algunas zonas, que han dejado incomunicadas varias localidades en la zona costera desde el sur de Gandia hasta Oliva por las inundaciones. Los servicios de emergencia están efectuando rescates en lancha y helicóptero y, aunque a las 10.00 ha bajado el nivel del aviso meteorológico de rojo a amarillo o naranja, las autoridades instan a la población a quedarse en casa. items.title: Otti signs laws toughening penalties for cultism, rape, kidnapping
items.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, on Monday signed four laws strengthening legal provisions against cultism, rape, sexual assault, kidnapping, child exploitation and vandalism of public infrastructure. The new legislation also provides for a sex offenders’ register, addresses offences involving electronic records and digital assets, and introduces restorative justice mechanisms to make offenders accountable for harm caused by their actions. Otti assented to the four bills passed by the eighth Abia State House of Assembly at a ceremony held at the Michael Okpara Auditorium, Umuahia. The laws are the Abia State Criminal Law No. 7 of 2026, the Administration of Criminal Justice Law No. 6 of 2026, the Restorative Justice Law No. 8 of 2026 and the Abia State University Amendment No. 2 Law No. 4 of 2026. Explaining the crime-fighting provisions, the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Mr Ikechukwu Uwanna, said the new Criminal Law strengthened measures against unlawful societies and secret cults by addressing membership, sponsorship, meetings and the management of such groups. He said the provisions extended beyond educational institutions to communities, widening the scope of the state’s response to cult-related activities. The law also provides sanctions for vandalising government infrastructure and dealing in stolen public assets, while strengthening legal protections against rape, sexual assault, sexual harassment and spousal violence. Uwanna said the legislation recognised both male and female rape victims and provided for a sex offenders’ register to promote accountability. Other provisions target kidnapping, child exploitation, corporate responsibility and offences involving electronic records and digital assets. The Attorney-General said the reforms were informed by public concerns over cult violence, kidnapping, the destruction of public facilities, sexual violence and delays in criminal proceedings. Otti vows strict enforcement Speaking during the signing ceremony, Otti said his administration was determined to ensure strict compliance with the new laws, noting that gaps in existing legislation had sometimes constrained the enforcement of government policies. The governor lamented that some existing laws did not prescribe sufficiently stringent consequences for certain offences, citing illicit drug consumption as an example. He argued that demand for illicit drugs sustained their supply, insisting that the law should adequately address the role of consumers in the drug trade. Otti, however, acknowledged that enacting laws was only part of the task, assuring residents that his administration had the political will to enforce them. Earlier, the Speaker of the House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Emmanuel Emeruwa, said the legislature had followed the necessary procedures in passing the bills, describing them as important measures for strengthening governance and improving the administration of justice. Uwanna explained that the three justice-related laws addressed criminal conduct, procedures for handling criminal cases and mechanisms for repairing harm caused by crime. He said the broader sentencing options provided under the Criminal Law would allow for restitution where appropriate, enabling offenders to make amends for the consequences of their actions. The Attorney-General also disclosed that the government planned to translate the new laws into Igbo to make their provisions more accessible to residents. Abia varsity campus relocation On the Abia State University Amendment Law, Otti said the relocation of the Umuahia campus to the institution’s main campus at Uturu was intended to reduce administrative costs and enable students to benefit from infrastructure and other investments at the main campus. The governor commended the eighth House of Assembly, members of the judiciary and other stakeholders for their contributions to the legislative process. The post Otti signs laws toughening penalties for cultism, rape, kidnapping appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: OCRTIS, un rempart contre la drogue et la criminalité au Niger…
items.description: La lutte contre la drogue est un combat pour la santé publique, la sécurité des familles et l’avenir de notre jeunesse. Au Niger, l’Office central de répression du trafic illicite des stupéfiants (OCRTIS), avec l’appui des Forces de défense et de sécurité, mène des opérations qui témoignent de l’importance de cette mission. Les résultats publiés par l’Agence nigérienne de presse (ANP) en 2026 montrent que les services antidrogue s’attaquent aussi bien aux réseaux internationaux qu’à la circulation des stupéfiants dans nos villes. Le 25 mai 2026, à Zinder, l’OCRTIS a réalisé une saisie record de 268,045 kilogrammes de cocaïne, répartis en 233 briques dissimulées sous la remorque d’un camion en provenance d’Accra, au Ghana. Huit personnes ont été interpellées. Cette opération témoigne de l’importance des investigations pour combattre les réseaux transnationaux. Source ANP Le 21 juin 2026, à Illéla, les agents ont saisi 263 000 comprimés d’ecstasy dans un véhicule en provenance de Cotonou, au Bénin. Six personnes ont été interpellées. Cette intervention montre l’importance des contrôles routiers pour empêcher l’acheminement de drogues à travers le territoire nigérien. Source ANP À Niamey, le 15 août 2026, l’opération « Tamisée » a mobilisé les forces de sécurité dans les cinq communes de la capitale, aux points de contrôle routiers et sur les berges du fleuve Niger. Selon l’ANP, 182 conducteurs ont été contrôlés, dont 25 testés positifs à des substances psychoactives. L’opération a également conduit à l’interpellation de 331 personnes, dont 27 mineurs, et à la saisie de plusieurs produits stupéfiants. Source ANP Le renforcement des moyens accompagne ces interventions. En avril 2026, trois vedettes rapides ont été remises à la brigade fluviale antidrogue de l’OCRTIS afin de renforcer la surveillance du fleuve Niger et de mieux lutter contre les trafics par voie fluviale. Source Le Sahel Autre résultat significatif, le 11 juillet 2026 à Tahoua, une importante quantité de stupéfiants saisis a été incinérée. Le bilan publié par l’ANP mentionne notamment 1 055 000 comprimés d’ecstasy, plus de 554 kilogrammes de cannabis et des dizaines de milliers de comprimés d’autres substances. Cette destruction permet de retirer du circuit les produits concernés, conformément aux procédures applicables. Source ANP Concernant l’opération « Une rentrée scolaire sans drogue », annoncée pour les 17 et 18 octobre 2026 à Niamey, le bilan transmis fait état de 461 personnes interpellées, dont 54 mineurs recensés, et de la saisie de 7 250 comprimés de tramadol, de cannabis et d’autres produits. Ces chiffres restent à confirmer par une publication officielle accessible. Derrière ces résultats, il y a un enjeu essentiel. Chaque cargaison interceptée peut empêcher des substances dangereuses d’atteindre des consommateurs. Chaque réseau démantelé peut réduire les possibilités de distribution de stupéfiants et les risques de criminalité associés. Il faut rappeler qu’une interpellation ne constitue pas une condamnation. La lutte contre la drogue doit respecter les procédures judiciaires et s’accompagner de prévention, de sensibilisation dans les écoles et de soutien aux jeunes exposés à la consommation. Hommage aux agents de l’OCRTIS et à l’ensemble des Forces de défense et de sécurité pour leur engagement au service de la population. Leur travail mérite d’être reconnu, tout comme les efforts nécessaires pour renforcer les enquêtes, la coopération entre services et la prévention. La lutte contre la drogue est l’affaire de tous. Parents, éducateurs, autorités et citoyens ont chacun un rôle à jouer. Protéger nos enfants contre la drogue, c’est protéger leur santé, leur avenir et celui du Niger. Par Ousmane Jazy L’article OCRTIS, un rempart contre la drogue et la criminalité au Niger… est apparu en premier sur Tamtaminfo .

items.title: I’m stuck with NPP – Jeneral Ntatia
items.description: Comedian Prince Kwame Amoabeng has revealed that he feels stuck with the New Patriotic Party (NPP) after campaigning for the party during the 2020 general elections. During the elections, he faced backlash for publicly declaring his support for the party. However, he said the criticism did not bother him because of the environment in which he grew up. He later explained that his decision to support the NPP was largely driven by its Free Senior High School (Free SHS) policy, citing his passion for education. In a recent interview with Nikki Samonas on Joy Prime , the comedian stated that his support for the party has left him feeling stuck with it, as the Free SHS policy played a major role in enabling his youngest sibling to complete senior high school without paying tuition fees. “I believe that Free SHS was something that really put people on; students went to school and that’s the reason I got love for it. Our last born went to Labone Senior High School for free. Had it not been it, probably our last born may not have been able to go to school because it wasn’t easy. So I decided that for all children to go to school, then let me go for NPP and I’m stuck there,” he said. For Ntatia, the criticism stemmed from people’s lack of understanding of his circumstances, as life became increasingly difficult following the loss of both parents. He had to take responsibility for his younger siblings’ education and upkeep. He revealed that he began caring for his siblings while still at university and could not bring himself to abandon a policy he believed would help ease his financial burden. “People don’t understand, by then my parents were gone and Free SHS really helped.” He also urged Ghanaians to vote for the NPP’s flagbearer, Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, in the 2028 general elections.

items.title: Sebta et Melilla : appel à un dialogue responsable pour mettre fin au litige territorial
items.description: Après la récente visite effectuée par le Roi Felipe VI d'Espagne aux deux villes occupées de Sebta et Melilla, un vaste rassemblement d'acteurs de la société civile marocaine est monté au créneau pour dénoncer une « provocation » , mais aussi prôner le dialogue serein et responsable . Dans un communiqué conjoint, des dizaines d'organisations des droits de l'homme, d'associations civiles, ainsi que de figures politiques, culturelles, médiatiques et artistiques ont exhorté les forces démocratiques et de défense des droits humains en Espagne et en Europe à s'engager dans un dialogue responsable afin de clore définitivement ce différend historique et de servir la justice, la paix et la coexistence entre les deux peuples. Les signataires ont fermement dénoncé cette démarche de la Couronne espagnole, la qualifiant de provocation politique délibérée envers le peuple marocain et de perpétuation d'une logique coloniale contraire aux principes de bon voisinage et de respect mutuel. Le texte souligne que ce déplacement envoie des signaux impérialistes révélant une contradiction flagrante entre le discours européen prônant la liberté et l'anticolonialisme et le maintien dans les faits de reliques de l'histoire. « Les relations maroco-espagnoles, bien que fondées sur des intérêts communs et les exigences du bon voisinage, doivent impérativement reposer sur le respect mutuel et la clarté dans le traitement des dossiers en suspens », ont souligné les entités signataires, annonçant à cet égard, leur intention de mener des consultations et d'assurer une coordination étroite avec les acteurs civils nationaux et les composantes de la communauté marocaine résidant à l'étranger, en vue de élaborer un programme d'action pacifique et responsable dédié à la défense des revendications historiques du Royaume sur les deux villes. Tout en réaffirmant l'appartenance marocaine irrévocable de Sebta, Melilla et des îles avoisinantes sous occupation, les entités signataires ont rejeté toute tentative d'imposer un fait accompli colonial. Elles ont appelé l'État marocain à adopter une stratégie nationale claire pour défendre ses droits historiques et souverains par des moyens politiques, diplomatiques et juridiques pacifiques. Cette prise de position collective réunit des organisations de premier plan, parmi lesquelles la Coalition marocaine des instances des droits de l'homme, la Ligue marocaine pour la défense des droits de l'homme, l'Association marocaine des droits humains, Transparency Maroc et le Forum marocain pour la vérité et la justice. La déclaration est également appuyée par les anciens bâtonniers Abderrahmane Benameur et Abderrahim Jamaï, aux côtés de Khadija Ryadi, militante emblématique et lauréate du Prix des Nations Unies pour la cause des droits de l'Homme, le bâtonnier Abderrahmane Allali, président de l'Observatoire marocain des prisons, l'ancien ministre et avocat au barreau de Casablanca Mustapha Ramid, ainsi qu'Ahmed Marzouki, écrivain et ancien détenu de Tazmamart, outre de nombreux autres juristes, journalistes et intellectuels de renom. Cette protestation unanime fait écho à d'autres réactions au niveau national, notamment celle du Groupe de travail national pour la Palestine, qui a qualifié la visite d'atteinte à la souveraineté nationale rappelant qu'il s'agit d'une question de décolonisation inaliénable, ainsi que de l'Alliance de la Gauche, qui a dénoncé une escalade unilatérale contraire au droit international. The post Sebta et Melilla : appel à un dialogue responsable pour mettre fin au litige territorial appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Christiane Amanpour to leave CNN after four decades as Ellison era begins
items.description: CNN’s chief international anchor Christiane Amanpour will leave next year, after 43 years with the network, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters on Monday. The news channel has recently come under the ownership of Skydance, whose Chief Executive Officer David Ellison has faced criticism over his stewardship of CBS News . “After thinking carefully for several months … I’ve decided to separate from CNN , my partner of 43 fantastic years,” Amanpour said in a video statement, joking that it was “longer than many marriages”. She added that her daily show on CNN would conclude at the end of this year, but that she would continue hosting ‘Amanpour’ once a week through to June 2027. Thanking her TV crew and colleagues, Amanpour highlighted that it was the “teams and the camaraderie we built that counts so much”. Amanpour, whose first major assignment was covering the first Gulf War, went on to report on conflicts in Bosnia, Rwanda, Afghanistan, Ukraine and Iran. Skydance, formerly Paramount Skydance, completed its $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros Discovery earlier this month, bringing CNN and CBS News under one roof. CNN chief Mark Thompson and CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss kept their roles, with both reporting to Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz. Lawmakers have criticised Ellison for tailoring news coverage at CBS News to favour US President Donald Trump.

items.title: Where have Ghana’s fireflies and antlions gone?
items.description: From fireflies that lit up the night to antlions known locally as kokroko, familiar insects appear to be disappearing from some Ghanaians’ everyday experiences. Scientists say understanding what is happening, and why, is an important first step towards protecting insect life. For many Ghanaians, childhood memories of the outdoors include tiny lights flickering through the darkness as fireflies moved across the night, and small, funnel-shaped pits in sandy ground where antlions, locally known as kokroko , lay in wait for their prey. These encounters were once familiar sights for some people. Today, however, some Ghanaians say they rarely see these insects, raising questions about whether their populations are declining and what might explain their apparent disappearance. While these observations do not, on their own, establish a nationwide decline, they point to a question worth investigating: what has happened to the insects that once formed part of everyday life in many communities? During an interview conducted as part of my UKmeet Fellowship, Dr Lawrencia Osae-Nyarko, a researcher at the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)-Ghana, raised concerns about declining insect populations and identified chemical spraying as a possible contributing factor. Her concerns draw attention to a wider environmental question: could some of the chemicals used to protect crops also be affecting insects that play important roles in sustaining ecosystems? Beyond the disappearance of familiar insects Insects are often overlooked in conversations about environmental protection, but their contributions extend well beyond the immediate surroundings in which they are found. Some insects help pollinate plants, recycle nutrients and maintain soil health. Others provide natural pest control by feeding on organisms that damage crops. Insects also serve as food for birds, reptiles and other animals, making them an important part of wider food webs. Fireflies are known for their bioluminescence, the natural process that allows them to produce light. Depending on the species, this ability plays a role in attracting mates and communicating. Antlions, meanwhile, are predators whose larvae often construct distinctive funnel-shaped pits in loose sand to trap small insects. They contribute to the natural regulation of insect populations. A reduction in the populations of particular species could therefore have consequences beyond the loss of familiar sights and childhood memories. However, the extent of any decline in Ghana’s firefly and antlion populations remains a question that requires systematic investigation. Could chemical spraying be part of the problem? Pesticides are widely used to protect crops against insects and other organisms that threaten agricultural production. When applied appropriately, they can help farmers manage pests and reduce crop losses. But some pesticides can also affect non-target organisms, including insects that are not responsible for crop damage. The effects depend on factors such as the chemical used, its concentration, how frequently it is applied, the method of application and the organisms exposed. Chemical spraying is therefore one possible factor to investigate when examining reports of declining insect populations. Other potential contributors include habitat loss, urbanisation, changes in land use, pollution and changes in environmental conditions. Establishing whether any of these factors is responsible for changes in firefly or antlion populations in Ghana would require evidence from field observations and scientific research. Dr Osae-Nyarko’s concerns raise an important starting point, but determining the scale of the problem and its causes will require more than personal recollections. Finding answers through science Understanding what is happening to Ghana’s insects will require researchers to establish a reliable picture of their populations and distribution. Regular insect surveys across different locations could help determine which species are present, where they occur and whether their numbers are changing over time. Researchers could also investigate the relationship between pesticide use and insect populations by examining the chemicals used in different settings, their application patterns and their potential effects on non-target species. Such work could help distinguish the effects of chemical exposure from those of habitat changes and other environmental pressures. Where pesticide use is found to pose risks to beneficial insects, practical alternatives may include integrated pest management. This approach combines different methods of controlling crop pests, including monitoring pest populations, using biological controls and applying chemical treatments selectively when necessary. The objective is not to eliminate the use of pesticides altogether, but to manage pests while reducing unnecessary harm to other organisms. Farmers, researchers, environmental authorities and communities could all contribute to efforts to understand and protect insect populations. A question worth answering For those who remember fireflies illuminating the night or discovering kokroko pits in sandy patches, the question of where these insects have gone carries a personal significance. Yet the issue extends beyond nostalgia. It raises questions about the health of the environments in which people live, grow food and interact with nature. The first step is to establish whether these insects are declining, identify the areas and species affected, and investigate the factors that may be contributing to any changes. That evidence could then guide decisions on pesticide use, habitat protection and other measures to conserve insect diversity. Can science help explain what has happened to Ghana’s fireflies and antlions, and identify ways to protect them before they become increasingly rare sights? Answering that question begins with paying attention to the small creatures around us and taking seriously what their presence, or apparent absence, might tell us about the environment.

items.title: CNN anchor Christiane Amanpour to leave network after 43 years
items.description: CNN’s chief international anchor, Christiane Amanpour, has announced she will leave the organisation next year after more than four decades. “After many months of thought and a few sleepless nights, I have decided to separate from CNN, my partner of 43 fantastic years!” Amanpour said in a statement. The 68-year-old said she “looks forward to interesting new projects down the line, and will always be rooting for CNN and maintaining its history of independent journalism. Remember: always be truthful, not neutral”. CNN chairman Mark Thompson described her as “one of the most trusted and beloved journalists anywhere” and said the network will take time to celebrate her “before she departs next year”. Amanpour began working for CNN in 1983 as an assistant on the international news desk, and went on to become one of the network’s best-known correspondents, often reporting on conflicts and wars. She has presented her own nightly interview program on CNN International since 2009. Amanpour pictured covering the US-led peacekeeping operation in Mogadishu in 1992 In a memo to staff on Monday, Thompson wrote: “Christiane has thought carefully about this decision, and she and I have been discussing it for some months. “Like so many CNNers who will hear the news today, I’m very sorry to see her go, but I’ve come to accept that this is the right time for her, both personally and professionally. “In the meantime, on behalf of the entire CNN leadership team, I want to thank Christiane for 43 extraordinary years of remarkable journalism, loyalty and friendship,” he added. In her own statement, Amanpour said she wanted to thank “all the amazingly talented people I’ve worked with throughout this incredible journey. Especially my beloved show teams and field crews.” Amanpour reflected on her “very first big exciting assignment covering the First Gulf War, to the horrors of the Bosnian War, Rwanda, Afghanistan, Ukraine and Iran and all the points in between”. “It’s the teams and the camaraderie that counted so much,” she continued, “as we together battled to seek the facts, the evidence and the humanity, so that CNN could always broadcast the truth about the world and to the world, without fear nor favour.”

items.title: Audi A3 désossées à Alger : trois suspects, dont une femme, écroués
items.description: Les images avaient fait le tour des réseaux sociaux fin septembre dernier et indigné l’opinion publique. Elles ont été partagées par une femme choquée de découvrir son véhicule, une Audi A3 garée à l’extérieur, dépourvue de ses portières. Sur la vidéo, on pouvait voir un autre véhicule garé à proximité et qui a subi la même dégradation. La police a réagi avec célérité et a pu identifier et arrêter les auteurs du forfait, au nombre de trois, dont une femme. Audi A3 désossées à Alger : un vol minutieusement préparé et exécuté en un temps record Les faits se sont déroulés à la cité Garidi, à Kouba (Alger). La victime a déposé plainte en date du 29 septembre, indique ce lundi 19 octobre le tribunal d’Hussein-Dey. Selon la même source, les suspects ont minutieusement planifié le vol, ce qui leur a permis de le commettre « avec une grande précision et en un temps record », sans attirer l’attention ni laisser de traces, en mettant à profit le facteur de l’obscurité et l’absence de passants. Trois suspects écroués Les auteurs du vol ont été identifiés. Il s'agit des dénommés Douma Youssef, 33 ans, Nahi Mehdi, 29 ans, et Othmani Kahina, 28 ans. Arrêtés, ils ont été présentés devant le tribunal d’Hussein-Dey qui les a placés en détention provisoire. Les mis en cause sont poursuivis pour « association de malfaiteurs en vue de commettre un vol avec circonstances aggravantes, effraction et nuit, utilisation d’un véhicule à moteur », ainsi que pour le délit de mise en circulation d’un véhicule muni d’une plaque d’immatriculation falsifiée. L’article Audi A3 désossées à Alger : trois suspects, dont une femme, écroués est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: GES Director-General to face parliamentary committee over Obuasi SHTS abuse allegations
items.description: The Director-General of the Ghana Education Service (GES), Professor Ernest Kofi Davis, will be expected to appear before a parliamentary committee to answer questions about the Service’s handling of sexual abuse allegations at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), the MP for Salaga South, Zuwera Mohammed Ibrahimah, has said. The MP said the Service must explain why it had not provided clear information about the findings of its investigation and the action it intends to take beyond suspending the headteacher accused of abusing students. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Monday, October 19, she criticised what she described as the GES’s silence on the matter, despite reportedly receiving the investigation report weeks before JoyNews published its findings. “The GES will appear before the parliamentary committee, and the Director-General of the Ghana Education Service will appear to come and explain the attitude,” she said. She questioned the Service’s response to the allegations, arguing that earlier intervention could have prevented the situation from escalating. “ The attitude of the GES is scarier than what has happened,” she said. The MP also questioned whether the Service had taken adequate steps to protect students and ensure accountability, insisting that education officials had questions to answer over their handling of the complaints. She said the allegations had been brought to the attention of authorities more than a year ago, yet the matter had not been adequately resolved. According to her, a petition from one of the girls was presented to the municipal assembly around the time the current Municipal Chief Executive assumed office, raising concerns about why the complaints had not prompted decisive action earlier. She also questioned the outcome of interventions by local government officials, including the Kumasi mayor, saying the circumstances surrounding their engagement with the headteacher needed to be examined. The MP said the proposed parliamentary inquiry would provide an opportunity for relevant stakeholders to explain their roles and help establish why the allegations were not addressed earlier. Her comments follow a JoyNews investigative documentary by Manasseh Azure Awuni detailing allegations of sexual abuse involving students at the school and raising questions about the handling of complaints by school authorities and other stakeholders.

items.title: Kofi Tonto demands answers from Ablakwa over alleged errors in South Africa evacuation records
items.description: Kofi Tonto, spokesperson for Employment on the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Policy Committee, has called on Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa to address alleged discrepancies in records covering the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa. Mr Tonto has raised concerns over entries containing questionable dates of birth, duplicate passport numbers and alleged multiple payments to beneficiaries, insisting that the Minister must provide clear explanations to the concerns raised by the Minority in Parliament. In a Facebook post, Mr Tonto questioned the adequacy of Mr Ablakwa’s public response to the controversy, arguing that the issues identified in the documentation provided by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs remained unresolved. He cited examples of individuals whose dates of birth were reportedly recorded as falling in 2034 and 2036, as well as another entry indicating February 31, 1990, a date that does not exist. He argued that the discrepancies warranted clarification from the Ministry to establish whether they resulted from administrative errors or other problems with the records. Mr Tonto also alleged that the documents contained instances in which different individuals were listed under identical passport numbers and that some beneficiaries appeared to have received duplicate payments. He maintained that the concerns went beyond simple data-entry errors, given their potential implications for the accuracy of the evacuation records and the accounting of allowances paid to returnees. “The demand is simple; respond to the gaps in your own data. We are interested in answers not more questions,” he wrote. He further criticised the Minister’s handling of the controversy, stating: “Ablakwa should not think for a second that his bogus media gymnastics has exonerated him.” The dispute follows concerns raised by the NPP Minority in Parliament over passenger manifests and payment documentation for the evacuation exercise. Nana Asafo-Adjei Ayeh, Deputy Ranking Member of Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, previously said the Minority’s examination of documents provided by the Ministry revealed a difference between the official number of evacuees and the passengers identifiable in the flight records reviewed. According to the Minority, its assessment identified 1,173 passengers in the available documentation, compared with the Ministry’s reported total of 1,964 evacuees. The Minority has consequently called for clarification on the missing entries, the payment registers and the expenditure associated with the exercise.

items.title: « Ni Français, ni Algérien » : Karim Zéribi fustige Éric Zemmour après ses propos haineux sur les Maghrébins
items.description: Par son discours de haine débridé, Éric Zemmour pousse, depuis plusieurs années, à la guerre civile en France. Les émeutes de samedi 17 octobre ont constitué une autre occasion pour lui de cibler directement les Français d’origine maghrébine et africaine, qu'il a qualifiés de « barbares ». Évidemment, le média qui laisse passer ce genre de propos, c'est LCI . Sur la chaîne qualifiée d’extrémiste par l’auteur, Éric Zemmour ne s'est pas retenu dimanche 18 octobre, au lendemain d’une journée d'émeutes dans toute la France. « Ce que nous avons vu hier, c’est le véritable visage du grand remplacement. Il a une apparence : une horde de barbares maghrébins et africains qui entrent dans les villes », a-t-il dit. Sabrina Sebaihi saisit le procureur contre Éric Zemmour Le fondateur du parti Reconquête en a aussi profité pour mélanger les genres et mettre en cause la politique mémorielle d’Emmanuel Macron, notamment avec l'Algérie. « Ce n'est pas la misère qui unit ces émeutiers. C'est leur haine de la France. Ils vivent dans le même bain culturel et religieux, et ils répètent que la France les a colonisés et volés. Tant que la France s'excusera, ils se croiront en droit de se venger », a encore estimé Zemmour. Des propos qui, évidemment, ne passent pas et suscitent une vive indignation et des signalements à la justice. « Je saisis le procureur de la République au titre de l’article 40 du Code de procédure pénale », a annoncé la députée écologiste Sabrina Sebaihi. « Zemmour ne dérape pas. Il vomit son racisme sur LCI . Qualifier les Maghrébins et les Africains de horde de barbares, c’est déshumaniser des populations entières. Ces propos ne doivent pas rester impunis », a écrit sur X l'élue d’origine algérienne. Zemmour ne dérape pas. Il vomit son racisme sur LCI. Qualifier les Maghrébins et les Africains de « horde de barbares », c’est déshumaniser des populations entières. Ces propos ne doivent pas rester impunis. Je saisis le procureur de la République au titre de l’article 40 du Code de procédure pénale. — Sabrina Sebaihi (@SabrinaSebaihi) October 18, 2026 « Éric Zemmour tient des propos de guerre civile » Thomas Portes, député de La France insoumise (LFI), a lui aussi annoncé qu’il saisissait le procureur contre Éric Zemmour qui, estime-t-il, « déverse une fois de plus sa haine raciste sur les plateaux télé ». « Nous ne laisserons rien passer face aux racistes et à leurs complices médiatiques », a-t-il promis. Antoine Léaument, du même parti, va droit au but et accuse Zemmour de pousser à la guerre civile. « Honte à Éric Zemmour qui tient des propos de guerre civile sur LCI », a écrit le député sur X . Pour Léaument, Éric Zemmour « incite à la haine contre les personnes perçues comme maghrébines » et son but est de « déclencher des violences racistes comme ses amis avaient réussi à le faire au Royaume-Uni ». « La violence, c’est Zemmour », a-t-il assuré. Honte à Éric Zemmour qui tient des propos de guerre civile sur LCI . Il incite à la haine contre les personnes perçues comme maghrébines. La violence, c’est Zemmour. — Antoine Léaument (@ALeaument) October 18, 2026 Karim Zéribi a également réagi à la réponse d’Alexandre Benalla, qui a rappelé à Éric Zemmour ses origines algériennes. « Cher Alexandre Benalla, évite de confondre la diaspora algérienne avec un individu frappé de psychiatrie identitaire ! Des millions de Franco-Algériens se sentent insultés par cet amalgame. Ce personnage n’est ni Français ni Algérien : sa seule patrie, c’est le racisme et l’islamophobie ! », a-t-il écrit sur X . items.title: Adu-Boahene’s lawyers ask High Court to strike out alleged fabricated claims in Deputy AG’s submissions
items.description: Lawyers for former National Signals Bureau (NSB) Director-General Kwabena Adu-Boahene have asked the High Court to expunge portions of the prosecution’s written arguments in opposition to the accused persons’ submission of no case to answer, alleging that they contain fabricated statements and misrepresentations of evidence presented during the trial. The application, filed on October 19, 2026, by defence counsel Samuel Atta Akyea, challenges sections of the Deputy Attorney-General’s submissions filed on October 9, 2026. The defence argues that some passages attribute statements to prosecution witnesses that were never made and refer to facts that were not established in evidence or recorded in the proceedings. In an affidavit supporting the application, the accused persons contend that the prosecution introduced invented statements and paragraphs that do not exist in the court record. They maintain that legal submissions must be based strictly on evidence admitted during proceedings and that neither party can introduce new evidence through arguments presented by counsel. Defence disputes prosecution’s account of witness testimony A major issue raised in the application concerns Exhibits X and 11, which the prosecution allegedly described as forged or fabricated documents. The defence disputes the attribution of such testimony to prosecution witnesses PW2 and PW4, arguing that neither witness testified that the exhibits were forged. The lawyers further point to the chronology of the proceedings, noting that PW2 was discharged on April 27, 2026, while Exhibit X was admitted through PW4 on June 22, 2026. According to the defence, this sequence undermines any suggestion that PW2 testified about the exhibit during her appearance in court. The application also challenges the prosecution’s alleged reliance on PW2’s testimony to argue that the NSB had no contract with ISC Holdings Limited for the supply of a cyber-defence system. The defence maintains that the witness acknowledged the processing and payment of an invoice connected to the system, including milestones relating to delivery and acceptance. Additionally, the lawyers dispute the claim attributed to PW2 that the NSB did not know BNC Communications Bureau Limited or its bank account. They argue that the witness’s comments about the account were based on her assumption that it was an operational account and should not be presented as establishing the broader claim advanced by the prosecution. GH¢49.1m transaction at centre of dispute The defence has also challenged the prosecution’s alleged interpretation of evidence concerning GH¢49.1 million linked to the cyber-defence system transaction. According to the application, the prosecution’s submissions suggest that PW3 testified that the entire amount was spent on the accused persons, their friends, associates and family members rather than for an official or approved purpose. The defence argues that this characterisation does not reflect the witness’s actual testimony. It states that PW3 identified ISC International Security Consultants Holdings Limited as the beneficiary of Exhibits 19 and 20 and read the remittance information as relating to the procurement of a cyber-defence system under invoice NSC006. The lawyers contend that this evidence does not support the prosecution’s alleged description of the transaction. Another point of contention involves Exhibit H, which the prosecution allegedly cited to support claims that money was transferred from a company’s bank account to Adu-Boahene’s mother for a building project in Kumasi. The defence argues that Exhibit H is a photograph of a building and not a bank statement, nor does it contain accounting annotations demonstrating that the alleged payments were made. It also refers to testimony attributed to PW4 acknowledging that no direct payments from the accounts analysed were made towards Dorchester Heights, the property identified in the proceedings as the Kumasi project. Defence wants disputed passages struck out In their supporting affidavit, the accused persons argue that a party cannot ask the court to rely on facts that have not been established through evidence. They contend that introducing such material in written submissions amounts to giving evidence from the bar, which they maintain is impermissible under the applicable rules of evidence and court procedure. The defence is therefore asking the High Court to strike out the specific passages identified in the application. Alternatively, it wants the court to disregard those portions when determining whether the accused persons have a case to answer. The application does not itself determine whether the disputed passages are inaccurate or whether the prosecution’s arguments are legally inadmissible. Those questions remain for the court to consider. Application comes ahead of ruling on no-case submission The latest motion follows the prosecution’s closure of its case on September 8, 2026. The accused persons filed their submission of no case to answer on September 25, 2026, before the prosecution submitted its opposition on October 9. A submission of no case to answer asks the court to assess whether the prosecution has presented sufficient evidence to require the accused persons to open their defence. The defence’s latest application raises a related procedural issue by challenging what it describes as inaccuracies and fabricated material in the prosecution’s written arguments. Its outcome could determine whether the contested passages will remain part of the material considered by the court as it evaluates the no-case submission. The High Court is being asked to ensure that its determination is based on the evidence properly placed on record and the parties’ arguments grounded in that evidence.

items.title: Diaspora AES au Sénégal : un soutien renouvelé à la marche souveraine de la Confédération…
items.description: En marge de son séjour à Dakar dans le cadre de la Réunion ministérielle du dialogue sur la coopération entre la Communauté Économique des États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest et la Confédération des États du Sahel, la délégation ministérielle de la Confédération AES, a tenu, le dimanche 18 octobre 2026, une rencontre d’échanges avec la diaspora confédérale vivant au Sénégal. Les échanges fraternels étaient axés sur la marche souveraine de la Confédération AES, fruit de la vision éclairée des plus hautes Autorités des trois pays membres pour la prise en main de la destinée de l’espace confédéral tant au niveau de la défense et de la sécurité que dans les domaines de la diplomatie et du développement durable. Au regard des acquis importants dans la lutte contre le terrorisme, l’affirmation de la Confédération AES sur la scène internationale et la promotion du développement endogène dans l’espace confédéral, la diaspora AES au Sénégal a renouvelé son soutien total à la vision et aux efforts de nos plus hautes Autorités dans leur lutte pour la souveraineté, la dignité et la prospérité partagée. S’agissant de ses doléances et préoccupations sur des questions administratives, notamment consulaires, les Ministres ont relevé les efforts de nos différentes administrations centrales et missions diplomatiques et consulaires pour prendre en charge les besoins spécifiques de nos compatriotes établis à l’extérieur. A cet égard, ils ont rappelé que la satisfaction des aspirations de nos concitoyens où qu’ils se trouvent, demeure l’objectif central de nos plus hautes Autorités. Tout en invitant les compatriotes de nos trois pays, fortement mobilisés à cette circonstance, à participer davantage à la construction confédérale, les Ministres les ont exhortés au respect de la règlementation du pays d’accueil et à être des modèles de l’intégration fraternelle et solidaire, incarnée par la Confédération AES. items.title: IA et justice pénale : Hicham Balaoui prône un cadre éthique et respectueux des droits de l'Homme
items.description: L'approche de l’intelligence artificielle (IA) au sein de l'institution judiciaire ne saurait se cantonner à la simple exploitation de ses capacités techniques, elle exige avant tout une compréhension rigoureuse de ses limites et la mise en place de garde-fous éthiques infranchissables. C'est en substance le message livré ce lundi à Fès par Hicham Balaoui, Procureur général du Roi près la Cour de Cassation et Président du Ministère public. S'exprimant à l'ouverture d'une session de formation destinée aux responsables judiciaires des parquets sur le thème « Intelligence artificielle et droits de l’Homme », Balaoui a souligné l'urgence d'un encadrement juridique et normatif adapté, à l'heure où la transformation numérique bouscule les paradigmes de la justice pénale, du droit à la défense, de la vie privée et des garanties d'un procès équitable. Si les algorithmes et les outils décisionnels offrent désormais des perspectives inédites pour la détection des infractions, l'analyse prédictive, le ciblage des fraudes et l'efficacité des enquêtes, le patron du Parquet général a mis en garde contre les vulnérabilités inhérentes à ces technologies. « L’intelligence artificielle, en dépit de ses précieux atouts opérationnels, recèle des risques majeurs susceptibles de porter atteinte à l'intégrité des droits fondamentaux et des libertés individuelles s'ils ne sont pas soumis à un contrôle humain strict », a-t-il dit. Programmée dans le cadre de l'exécution du plan stratégique 2026-2028 de la Présidence du Ministère public, singulièrement son axe dédié à la consolidation des liberté, cette rencontre inaugure un cycle national de formations régionales visant à renforcer les compétences des magistrats face aux mutations technologiques. Organisée conjointement avec le Centre de Genève pour la gouvernance du secteur de la sécurité (DCAF), cette session bénéficie de l'expertise de son représentant, Samir Marmouri, qui a salué les efforts continus du Royaume pour aligner la gouvernance de son système judiciaire sur les meilleurs standards internationaux. Pendant deux jours, les responsables judiciaires examineront l'application des grands textes de référence mondiaux, notamment la Recommandation de l'UNESCO sur l'éthique de l'intelligence artificielle (2021), les principes de l'OCDE sur l'IA (2019), et la Convention-cadre du Conseil de l'Europe sur l'IA, les droits de l'Homme, la démocratie et l'État de droit (2024). Les travaux s'articuleront autour d'ateliers pratiques axés sur la protection des données personnelles, la souveraineté de la décision judiciaire, les mécanismes de responsabilisation et la préservation des garanties procédurales face aux cybercriminalités émergentes. The post IA et justice pénale : Hicham Balaoui prône un cadre éthique et respectueux des droits de l'Homme appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Saudi Arabia: Man Executed for Childhood Offenses
items.description: Click to expand Image Men hold placards bearing portraits of a prominent Shia Muslim cleric, Nimr al-Nimr, whose execution sparked demonstrations in 2016 by the country's minority Shia citizens against systematic governmental discrimination. Some of the alleged child offenders currently on trial were accused of attending similar protests. © 2016 STR/AFP via Getty Images (Beirut) – Saudi authorities announced on October 17, 2026, that they had executed Hassan Zaki al-Faraj, who was convicted of crimes allegedly committed when he was a 14-year-old boy, Human Rights Watch said today. The Supreme Court has also apparently upheld the death sentence of another man, Yousef al-Manasif, who was convicted of crimes allegedly committed when he was 15 and 16, putting him at risk of imminent execution. At least three other men convicted of alleged crimes committed as children are on death row, despite allegations of torture, forced confessions, and prolonged solitary confinement. “The execution of Hassan al-Faraj is unconscionable compounded by alleged torture-tainted evidence and a well-documented record of unfair trials,” said Joey Shea, senior Saudi Arabia researcher at Human Rights Watch. “With the Supreme Court’s recent decision, Yousef al-Manasif is also at serious risk of execution.” The death sentence for al-Manasif was recently upheld by the Supreme Court, the European Saudi Organisation for Human Rights (ESOHR) reported. In October and November 2022, Saudi Arabia’s notorious Specialized Criminal Court handed down death sentences to al-Manasif and al-Faraj, as well as Ali al-Mabyook, Jawad Qureiris, Ali al-Subaiti, and Mahdi al-Mohsen for alleged terrorism crimes they committed as children, according to a report by the ESOHR and court documents. Saudi authorities arrested al-Faraj on November 27, 2017, held him in solitary confinement for six months, and charged him with various counterterrorism offenses, including one allegedly committed when he was 14, which relates to meeting and developing friendships with other detained and wanted individuals, based on the charge sheet and court documents. The Specialized Criminal Court sentenced him to death on November 3, 2022, despite allegations that he had been tortured and forced to sign the confession on which the conviction was based, his defense said. Court documents reviewed by Human Rights Watch show that authorities arrested al-Manasif on April 6, 2017, and al-Mabyook on January 29, 2018. Al-Manasif was arrested for protesting Saudi authorities’ treatment of its Shia minority and attending funeral processions in 2011 and 2012 when he was 15 and 16, according to the ESOHR and United Nations experts. Al-Mabyook was arrested for attending funeral processions before he turned 18, ESOHR and court documents said. The court convicted and sentenced them to death on November 2, 2022, under broad and vague counterterrorism laws based almost exclusively on confessions that their defense alleges were obtained under torture, the documents showed. The authorities did not inform al-Manasif of his charges until months after his arrest or provide him with legal representation during his interrogation and held him in pretrial detention for over two years, including six months in solitary confinement, the documents show. Both al-Manasif and al-Mabyook appealed to the Appellate Chamber of the Specialized Criminal Court on March 19, 2025. The appeals were based on them both having been under 18 when the alleged offenses were committed, the court documents said. On August 26, 2025, the appellate court rejected that defense, referring to the dates in their confessions, despite allegations that the confession was obtained under torture. Saudi authorities arrested Qureiris on December 31, 2020, court documents say. Saudi authorities charged him under the counterterrorism law for alleged offenses at the ages of 15 and 17. The Specialized Criminal Court convicted and sentenced him to death on November 5, 2022, despite allegations of severe beatings during interrogation to make him sign a confession, the documents say. Qureiris was also held in solitary confinement for 270 days to force the confession, according to the documents. The decision was submitted to the same court for review on November 12, 2025, where Qureiris stated that he did not commit any of the alleged offenses except participating in a protest in 2010 when he was 15, court documents showed. The court approved his death sentence on March 2, 2025. The UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention concluded in November 2024 that the detentions of al-Manasif, al-Faraj, and Qureiris were arbitrary and based on the men’s exercise of their right to free speech when they participated in protests against Saudi Arabia’s treatment of the country’s Shia minority. On April 9, 2026, Saudi authorities executed Ali al-Subaiti for alleged crimes committed when he was 12, according to the Saudi Press Agency. On October 23, 2017, Saudi authorities arrested al-Subaiti, who was then 19, and charged him under counterterrorism provisions including joining and financing a terrorist organization and attempting to undermine the social fabric and national security by inciting protests, according to the charge sheet. The charges included participating in a demonstration when he was 12 and “covering up for terrorists” when he was 17. The court sentenced al-Subaiti to death on October 17, 2022, according to the ESOHR. Saudi Arabia’s Juvenile Law of 2018 and a 2020 executive order ended the use of the death penalty against individuals who were under 18 when the crime was committed, in cases that do not involve the 2017 counterterrorism law. In non-terrorism cases, the death penalty is replaced with a maximum 10-year prison sentence. Human Rights Watch has documented Saudi Arabia’s long-standing misuse of counterterrorism provisions to silence dissent. In 2025, Saudi Arabia executed Jalal al-Labbad and Abdullah al-Derazi, both accused of committing crimes as children, as part of the country’s unprecedented execution spree, despite calls from UN experts and rights groups to halt the executions. Human Rights Watch has documented long-standing due process violations in Saudi Arabia’s criminal justice system, including restricted or denied access to legal representation and forced confessions, making it highly unlikely that any of the eight men received a fair trial. The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, to which Saudi Arabia is a party, strictly prohibits the use of the death penalty for offenses committed by individuals under 18. Article 6(2) of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and article 6 of the Arab Charter on Human Rights oblige countries that use capital punishment to use it only for the “most serious crimes.” Human Rights Watch opposes the death penalty in all countries and circumstances due to its inherent cruelty and irreversibility. “Saudi Arabia’s execution spree, particularly for offenses by children, shows no signs of slowing down in 2026,” Shea said. “This underscores the urgent need for the international community to press the Saudi government to immediately halt executions and abolish the death penalty once and for all.”

items.title: Senate approves bill seeking blue passports for ex-lawmakers with incomplete term
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Senate on Monday passed a bill that sought to allow former lawmakers to have blue passports even if they had not served a full term in the National Assembly (NA) or Senate. In the same sitting, the House withdrew a bill seeking to allow the issuance of blue passports to dependent children under the age of 28 of ex-members of Parliament. Official blue passports are issued to key constitutional, government and judicial office holders, senior bureaucrats and their eligible dependents, allowing them visa-free entry to 55 countries, including 22 European countries. The bills pertaining to the blue passport were moved by Senator Abdul Qadir today. Of them, the House passed the amendment inserting a new Section 3-A in the Passports Act, 1974, which states that “a retired parliamentarian who has taken oath as a Member of the National Assembly (MNA) or the Senate, whether for a full term or for the remainder of the term of another member, shall, on such terms and conditions as may be prescribed, be entitled to retain and use the gratis official (blue) passport issued to him or her after ceasing to hold office”. The amendment also covers lawmakers who leave office before completing five years as an MNA or six years as a senator. At present, blue passports are issued to those ex-parliamentarians who remained a member of either House for at least one term, according to the Passport Rules 2021 . The statement of objects and reasons of the bill approved by the Senate states that the amendment “brings parity with the privileges available to other high-ranking officials and ensures uniform treatment of persons who have served the state at the highest level”. The bill has yet to be passed by the NA. The second bill, which sought to amend Section 12 of the Members of Parliament (Salaries and Allowances) Act, 1974 to provide that “an ex-member, the spouse of the ex-member and the dependent children of the ex-member below the age of 28 years shall be entitled to a gratis official (blue) passport”, was withdrawn after opposition by treasury members in the Senate. In July, the bill had been approved by the relevant Senate committee, with the government drawing backlash. After criticism of the bill, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry had assured that measures would be taken to ensure that the travel document was used for “only official duties” abroad and issued for a limited time in most cases. Speaking on blue passports in the Senate, Chaudhry said the number of these official passports issued in the country had been reduced from 75,000 to 45,000 after European countries and Canada raised reservations. Around 30,000 unnecessary and inactive blue passports had been cancelled, he said. “Security and dignity of passport is a matter of the dignity of people of Pakistan,” he remarked, noting that Pakistan also had agreements with other countries regarding blue and red passports. He said the government had no issue with parliamentarians themselves getting blue passports but had concerns over extending the facility to their families, explaining that a large number of blue passports resulted in other countries hesitating to offer visa-free access. He added that a bill would soon be moved to withdraw the blue passport facility available for the children of retired bureaucrats. Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar emphasised that blue passports should be regulated as they are meant for official business. “Let children make their own careers; respect is not built through blue passports,” he said. He also called for ending the six-year service requirement for Senate members to obtain official passports, saying the rules should be the same for members of the Senate and the NA. NA members became eligible for official passports after taking the oath, while senators had to complete their six-year term, he said, adding that a senator who resigned a few months before completing their term could lose eligibility for the passport. PML-N Senator Abid Sher Ali strongly criticised the requirement of a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the interior ministry for the issuance of blue passports to parliamentarians, saying it did not exist earlier. “Are we dacoits or terrorists that we need NOCs?” he said, terming the requirement a breach of privilege. He announced that he would move a privilege motion in this regard. ‘Assault on people’s mandate’ The Senate also witnessed a debate between the opposition and the treasury over the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Leader of the Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas termed the move an “assault on the people’s mandate”. “You robbed the people’s votes. Your own minister said the system has collapsed ,” he said, referring to comments made by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi about the governance system in the country requiring a reset. Speaking at the Pakistan Economic Summit in July, the interior minister had said the current “system” of governance had “collapsed”, and was fundamentally incapable of resolving the country’s problems. The opposition leader said what happened in KP was “sheer oppression” and could have been avoided. He also urged the government not to push people to the wall, saying, “You snatched the mandate from Bengalis and they separated. You have still not learned.” Abbas also sought a briefing on Yemen, noting that Parliament in 2015 had passed a resolution not to be part of the conflict in the Middle Eastern country. He said he had written to the prime minister and foreign minister asking them to mediate, instead of becoming part of the conflict. “This is a sensitive issue. Countries are economically devastated and we are going to be part of another war,” he said. In response, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said that emergency and governor’s rule were imposed in KP via a presidential order under Articles 233 and 234 of the Constitution, and were ratified by the Senate and National Assembly. “All steps have been taken in the interest of peace, stability and national interest,” he said. Additional input from APP

items.title: Parliament must summon stakeholders over Obuasi SHTS abuse – Salaga South MP
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Salaga South, Zuwera Mohammed Ibrahimah, is pushing for Parliament to summon key stakeholders to answer questions over allegations of sexual abuse involving students of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS). She said Parliament should investigate the handling of the allegations, including claims of attempts to prevent victims from pursuing justice and the possible roles played by school officials. Speaking on JoyNews ’ The Pulse on Monday, October 19, she has discussed with the chairperson of Parliament’s Gender Committee plans to present a statement on the floor of the House when Parliament resumes later in October. “I am discussing with the chairperson of the Gender Committee to put together a statement. Parliament is resuming, I think, towards at the end of the month. We will make a forceful statement on the floor of Parliament. We will expect our colleagues to support the recommendations we’ll be making in the statement, and we’ll be requesting the Right Honorable Speaker to refer the matter to a three-member committee, which will be the Gender, Children and Social Welfare Committee, the Education Committee, and the Committee on Human Rights of Parliament. We need to sit down and interrogate these matters, bring all stakeholders to Parliament to answer for what has gone on with the so far 19 brilliant girls,” she said. She added that she is particularly interested in the role of the housemistress, who she believes should be given the opportunity to explain her involvement in the matter. “I am interested in this housemistress. I’m interested in her story,” she said, calling for the allegations against her to be examined by an investigative body.” She also expressed concern about the psychological impact of the alleged abuse on the affected students, saying one victim had reportedly been unable to attend a meeting because of the trauma she had experienced. The MP said the investigation should establish what happened, identify any failures by school authorities and other stakeholders, and help restore confidence in the school system, particularly boarding schools. She further criticised what she described as an attempt to seek clemency for the suspended headteacher rather than ensure that the allegations were properly investigated and prosecuted. The calls follow a JoyNews investigative documentary by Manasseh Azure Awuni detailing allegations of sexual abuse at the school. Currently, the number of students who have come forward with allegations of sexual abuse involving the suspended headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School has risen from 16 to 19.

items.title: Achimota Golf Club raises GH¢96,960 for breast cancer equipment at Korle Bu
items.description: The Achimota Golf Club Ladies Section has raised GH¢96,960.44 towards the procurement of breast cancer equipment for Korle Bu Teaching Hospital through the 2026 Ocean Network Express (ONE) Pink Cup Tournament. The tournament was held on Saturday, October 17, at Achimota Golf Club in Accra, bringing together golfers, corporate sponsors and health advocates to promote breast cancer awareness and encourage early detection. Led by Lady Captain Kous Louanges Mang, the event exceeded its golfer participation target and more than doubled the contribution raised compared with the previous year. The funds were presented through a dummy cheque, with title sponsor Ocean Network Express (ONE) supporting the initiative to advance breast cancer care at the hospital. The event was attended by the Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, who joined efforts to highlight the importance of collective action in addressing breast cancer. Ahead of the tournament, the club organised a Community Pink Clinic on October 10, offering general health screening and promoting preventive healthcare. The Ladies Section acknowledged the support of its sponsors and partners, including ONE, KEK Group, Japan Motors, CalBank, Accelerate, Fairway Golf Academy, Destinations au Soleil, NZ Wine GH, Breast Care International, Claron Health International and Ignite Group. Media partners Metro TV, Joy News and Citi FM were also recognised for helping raise awareness of the initiative. Lady Captain Kous Louanges Mang expressed appreciation to the club’s leadership, organising committee, volunteers, participating golfers and other supporters who contributed to the success of the event. She stressed that the Pink Cup was a collective effort involving the entire club and its partners, rather than an initiative limited to the Ladies Section. The annual tournament combines golf with public health advocacy and fundraising, with the aim of supporting healthcare institutions and people affected by breast cancer.
