items.title: The Yamoransa model blueprint—Why Ghana must prioritise practical STEAM education
items.description: It is hard to believe that, in 2026, there are still young people in Ghana who have never touched a computer. For those of us in Accra and the country’s other urban centres, technology feels like it is everywhere, in our pockets, in our classrooms, on our desks, and woven into almost everything we do. But travel a few hours outside the capital, and the story changes completely. For millions of young people across Ghana and West Africa, especially those of basic and secondary school age, that same technology remains out of reach, and with it, the head start it gives their counterparts in the cities and abroad. We say often that STEAM education is the future. It is true. But that future only arrives through a deliberate, collective effort to put real tools in young people’s hands, not just the idea of technology, but the thing itself. For too many communities across Ghana and West Africa, that effort has been missing. It was missing ten years ago, and in far too many classrooms, it is still missing today. In 2018, a photo of a teacher in Sekyeredumase went viral: he had drawn the Microsoft Word interface on a blackboard, chalk standing in for a keyboard he had no way to give his students. It was a striking image, and an unacceptable one — yet it wasn’t an isolated case. Across the country, many teachers were, and still are, doing the very same thing: teaching a digital world with nothing but chalk and a board. It is worth asking, plainly, what kind of future leaders we are raising if this is how we are preparing them. When that image spread across social media, it struck a nerve nationally, and it echoed something the Helping Africa Foundation, together with IMPLEMENTERS, TECHAiDE and local partners, had already set out to fix two years earlier. In 2016, this partnership planted a seed in Yamoransa, a small community in Ghana’s Central Region, with a simple but ambitious idea: what if technology access wasn’t something young people had to wait for the government or the city to bring them, but something their own community could own? That idea became the Yamoransa Model for Sustainable Development, named after the town where it began. The model works because each partner carries a distinct piece of it: the Helping Africa Foundation provides the technology, IMPLEMENTERS manages the projects on the ground, TECHAiDE supplies the educational tools, including the ASANKA device that gives students offline access to learning materials even without an internet connection, and, in every community, a “promoter” — someone committed enough to the cause to provide the building that houses it all. Ten years on, that seed has grown into 19 fully equipped ICT and robotics labs — 17 of them spread across 15 regions in Ghana, with additional labs now serving communities in Liberia and The Gambia. Over 100,000 students have passed through these labs, gaining hands-on skills in robotics, 3D printing and digital literacy that once seemed unimaginable in their communities. These skills put them on a level footing with their peers anywhere else in the world. The model’s impact has not gone unnoticed. Over the years, it has counted President John Dramani Mahama, former President Nana Akufo-Addo, the Speaker of Parliament Rt. Hon. Alban Bagbin, former Second Lady Samira Bawumia, and a host of Members of Parliament among its promoters and champions — a rare, cross-partisan show of support that reflects just how urgent, and how solvable, this problem really is. On September 16, the Yamoransa Model marked this milestone with its 10th Anniversary Celebration, under the theme “A Decade of Impact: Empowering the Next Generation.” It was a moment to look back at everything a single community lab has grown into, and more importantly, a moment to look forward. Having now secured the Ghanaian government’s official backing, the model is more committed than ever to reaching the communities it hasn’t yet touched, in Ghana and beyond West Africa. The next decade of the Yamoransa Model cannot be built by the Helping Africa Foundation, IMPLEMENTERS and TECHAiDE alone. If the story of that teacher in Sekyeredumase moved you eight years ago, let it move you again today — because the real tragedy is not that it happened once, but that it is still happening, in classrooms the model hasn’t reached yet. The tools exist. The model works. What is needed now is more hands willing to help carry it forward.

CAN U17 UFOA-B: le Burkina croît en ses chances pour la qualification
items.description: L’entraineur des Etalons U17, Mamadou Zongo dit «Bébéto» reconnaît la force du Niger mais croit en ses garçons pour la qualification de la CAN U17 UFOAB, indique la Fédération burkinabè de football (FBF), ce lundi 19 octobre 2026. A la veille de la demi-finale face au Niger, prévue le mardi 20 octobre 2026, le sélectionneur national des Etalons U17, Mamadou Zongo dit Bébéto, «s'est montré prudent mais déterminé», en conférence de presse d'avant-match, selon la Fédération (FBF) ce lundi sur sa page Facebook. Le sélectionneur national des Etalons U17, Mamadou Zongo dit Bébéto Pour le technicien burkinabè, le Niger part avec un léger avantage au regard de ses prestations depuis le début du tournoi. «Je pense que le Niger est légèrement favori. Depuis le début de la compétition, j'ai trouvé cette équipe un peu au-dessus des autres», a-t-il reconnu. Conscient de l'enjeu, Bébéto assure que son groupe travaille à corriger ses lacunes, notamment dans la finition. «Ce n'est plus un match de poule, mais une rencontre à élimination directe. Il faudra savoir concrétiser nos occasions». La FBF souligne la même détermination chez le joueur Latif Traoré, qui rassure sur l'état d'esprit du groupe. «Le moral est au top. Le Niger veut se qualifier et nous aussi. L'équipe qui saura concrétiser ses occasions ira en finale», a-t-il déclaré. Rendez-vous donc le mardi à 19h30 pour un duel décisif avec, à la clé, une qualification pour la CAN U17. Par Wakat Séra L’article CAN U17 UFOA-B: le Burkina croît en ses chances pour la qualification est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Ronaldo receives 30-Day suspension and €255 fine for Portugal walkout
items.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has received a 30-day suspension and a €255 fine from the Portuguese football federation after leaving the Portugal squad during the most recent international break. The forward is 41. In late September, Ronaldo clashed with national team coach Jorge Jesus after spending the 2-1 international win over Norway on the bench. Ronaldo said Jesus had told him beforehand he would play for about half an hour. Ronaldo was told to warm up during the match but never got on. He felt Jesus had not taken him seriously and later said the coach had broken a second agreement. According to Ronaldo, Jesus had promised to explain the situation publicly at a press conference. Before Portugal faced Denmark, tensions rose and Ronaldo left the training camp. The Portuguese star later issued a lengthy public statement apologising to his team-mates and the supporters. He acknowledged that leaving the national team had to have consequences. Ronaldo went further, calling for an appropriate punishment in that statement. The captain said his status as a role model meant his actions should be judged strictly. Despite criticising Jesus’s conduct, he made clear he was ready to accept the consequences of his departure. A week and a half ago, the Portuguese federation announced formal disciplinary proceedings against the captain. Ronaldo would remain suspended until it decided his final punishment. The federation has now settled on a 30-day suspension and a €255 fine. Given Ronaldo’s salary, the fine is particularly low.

items.title: Dubréka : l’Institut supérieur des Arts Mory Kanté lance l’année universitaire 2026-2027
items.description: L’Institut supérieur des Arts Mory Kanté de Dubréka a officiellement lancé, ce lundi 19 octobre 2026, l’année universitaire 2026-2027. Au programme de cette nouvelle rentrée : l’élaboration de formations adaptées aux ambitions du projet Simandou 2040, l’expérimentation du Diplôme universitaire de technologie (DUT) et le renforcement des équipements pédagogiques. Après plusieurs semaines de vacances, étudiants et enseignants ont repris le chemin des salles de classe. Cette rentrée marque le début d’une nouvelle année universitaire, placée sous le signe du renforcement de l’offre de formation et de l’amélioration des conditions d’apprentissage. Pour l’année 2026-2027, la direction de l’établissement prévoit notamment l’élaboration de nouveaux programmes de formation en lien avec le projet Simandou 2040. L’expérimentation d’une formation sanctionnée par un Diplôme universitaire de technologie (DUT) figure également parmi les initiatives annoncées. Selon le directeur général, Pascal Ifono, ces dispositions visent à assurer le bon déroulement de l’année universitaire et à renforcer les capacités de formation de l’institution. Dans cette dynamique, des équipements pédagogiques et du matériel musical ont été acquis afin de favoriser les enseignements pratiques. Du côté du corps enseignant, cette reprise constitue une nouvelle occasion d’accompagner les étudiants dans leur parcours académique. Gervais Haba, chef de la section communication institutionnelle, évoque les perspectives qui s’ouvrent à l’établissement pour cette nouvelle année. Pour les nouveaux étudiants, cette rentrée représente une étape importante dans leur parcours. Orientée en première année de licence, Alimata Soumah découvre un environnement universitaire qui, reconnaît-elle, ne correspond pas entièrement à l’idée qu’elle s’en faisait avant son arrivée. La bibliothèque au cœur des perspectives L’accès aux ressources documentaires constitue également un enjeu pour l’établissement. Des efforts sont annoncés pour améliorer les conditions de recherche et d’apprentissage, notamment grâce à des partenariats avec d’autres universités et à l’acquisition d’ouvrages spécialisés en art dramatique et en cinéma. Avec ces différentes initiatives, l’Institut supérieur des Arts Mory Kanté de Dubréka entend consolider son offre de formation et améliorer l’encadrement des étudiants. Reste désormais à concrétiser les ambitions affichées, notamment en matière de diversification des formations, de disponibilité des ressources pédagogiques et d’amélioration des conditions d’apprentissage.

items.title: Kenya’s Fintech growth story: The challenge of scaling beyond success
items.description: Following my address at the Africa Fintech and Banking Summit in Nairobi on 8th October 2026, it is clear that while Kenya remains Africa’s undisputed fintech capital, the market narrative is fundamentally shifting. Widespread mobile money adoption, a vibrant innovation infrastructure, and a growing pipeline of technology-enabled financial services firms have turned Nairobi into a global launchpad. From digital lending and smart asset financing to embedded wealth solutions, fintech platforms are redrawing economic boundaries. Yet, initial market validation is merely step one; the true test lies in long-term execution. As tech scale-ups expand, they face complex regulatory frameworks, highly sophisticated cybersecurity threat landscapes, and rising consumer expectations. At the same time, institutional investors have turned away from the era of ‘growth at all costs,’ placing a premium on immediate pathways to profitability, clear corporate governance structures, and robust operational resilience. Long-term market leadership now belongs exclusively to firms that can balance continuous market-driven innovation with total operational discipline. 1. Core Strategic Hurdles & Structural Barriers To survive the transition from startup to structural scale-up, fintech leaders must proactively navigate four clear market gaps: The Funding Disconnect: While Kenyan startups secured nearly US$1 billion in 2025—a 52% year-on-year increase that accounts for roughly one-third of total continental funding—60% of this capital was structured as debt. Concurrently, early-stage seed transactions under US$100,000 fell by 23%. This signals a pronounced investor bias toward mature, asset-backed entities with predictable unit cash flows like d.light, Sun King, and M-KOPA. Early-stage players must prove solid unit economics from day one to defend baseline valuations. Proactive Regulatory Readiness: The regional regulatory perimeter is becoming more comprehensive. By mid-2026, the Central Bank of Kenya had licensed 252 digital credit providers, which collectively disbursed 8.37 million loans worth KSh150.56 billion by May 2026. Adherence to strict customer protection rules, data protection frameworks, and AML/CFT guidelines must be treated as core operational requirements rather than final compliance exercises. Additionally, the Virtual Asset Service Provider framework provides a clearer path for cross-border digital asset solutions. Specialized Technical Talent Gaps: Kenya’s roaring ICT sector contributes 9.24% to the national GDP and maintains a baseline talent registry of 330,000 IT professionals. However, deep specialization bottlenecks persist. Industry benchmarks demonstrate that the local cybersecurity workforce stands at just 1,700–2,000 active experts against an immediate institutional need of 40,000–50,000 specialists. Startups must leverage graduate talent funnels alongside flexible upskilling models for product, cyber-risk, and complex compliance positions. Systemic Structural Security Risks: The critical urgency for specialized cyber talent is highlighted by an unprecedented 202% quarter-on-quarter spike in regional digital attacks, which climbed to 2.5 billion distinct threats in early 2025. Scale metrics must emphasize active platform usage, systemic customer retention, and transaction uptime over mere user acquisition totals. 2. Designing an Optimal Capital Blueprint Fintech executives must dynamically match their funding structures to their precise lifecycle positions: Stage-Gated Capital Allocation: Deploy founder equity, startup accelerators, and corporate innovation grants for early validation. Transition to regional venture funds and family offices for initial geographic expansion, reserving structured venture debt or commercial bank lines for mature cash-flow stages. Local Market Validation First: International venture capital funds prioritize low Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) metrics, high retention curves, and controlled fraud metrics. Securing local operational traction and clear regulatory approvals drastically lowers external investor risk profiles. Investor Pool Diversification: Broaden your capitalization reach by systematically approaching commercial banks, pension funds, local investment clubs, and corporate partners alongside global DFIs and traditional impact investors. Deployment of Blended Finance: With debt facilities accounting for 41% of total African tech funding in 2025 (amounting to US$498 million in Kenya alone), combining core equity tranches with sovereign guarantees and receivables financing stretches a startup’s operational cash runway without over-diluting founders. Regulated Local Capital Markets: Eligible mid-market players should actively leverage licensed investment crowdfunding networks or evaluate commercial paper and private placement frameworks with structured legal counsel. Institutional Due Diligence Priming: Maintain an airtight virtual data room covering audited financial reports, complete intellectual property title trails, and clear tax histories. Ensure every capital tranche links directly to verifiable execution metrics to provide deep investor confidence in your long-term viability. 3. Technical Foundations for Global Elasticity To seamlessly handle exponential transaction volumes without service interruption, infrastructure must incorporate four architectural layers: Cloud-Native Elasticity: Migrate computing loads to auto-scaling containerized setups that provision processing bandwidth automatically during traffic spikes. Decoupled Microservices: Isolate application frameworks through clear API structures, allowing product modules to be updated or repaired independently without taking down the wider ecosystem. Automated Operations: Utilize Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) templates combined with real-time alerting systems to eliminate deployment mistakes and reduce system downtime. Embedded Engineering Controls: Hardcode end-to-end security measures, data masking routines, and unalterable ledger logging systems natively into the application codebase by design. 4. Integrating High-Velocity Ecosystem Partnerships Sustainable market dominance cannot be engineered in isolation. Value-creation requires deep network integration across traditional industries: Commercial Banking Networks: Establish secure gateway links with clearing banks to unlock deep financial accounts, instant domestic payment pipelines, and multi-generation institutional consumer trust. Telecommunications Networks: Deeply interconnect with dominant regional mobile network operators (e.g., Safaricom, Airtel) to easily tap into massive distribution agent networks and existing mobile wallet customer bases across urban and rural locations. Enterprise Merchants & E-Commerce: Directly embed contextual point-of-sale financing options, instant digital lending, and automated checkout options right inside partner enterprise commerce streams. Sovereign Identity Architecture: Programmatically anchor into official national identity registries and digital verification layers to streamline customer onboarding while stopping fraud vectors before processing. Executive Performance Indicators Matrix Operational Pillar Critical Metric Tracked Institutional Benchmark Target Growth Unit Economics Direct Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) optimization Lifetime Value (LTV) to CAC ratio tracking >= 3:1 Financial Transparency Annual systemic external corporate auditing Clean, unqualified historical financial statements Information Security Systemic cybersecurity workforce upskilling Structural migration toward zero-trust systems architecture Operational Capital Blended finance / Debt facility sourcing 18 to 24-month operational cash runway extension Systemic Reliability Automated operational performance tracking >= 99.99% core transaction processing uptime Strategic Outlook The future of Kenya and to a large extend African financial technology belongs to firms that build for resilience over speed. The final market leaders will not merely be the entities that secure the fastest customer acquisition spikes, but the most trusted, compliant, and structurally secure institutions capable of creating continuous economic value for consumers, investors, and regulators alike. Disclaimer: The views expressed are entirely personal and do not represent those of the author’s employer or any affiliated institution. About the Author Carl Odame-Gyenti, PhD, is the author of Dare to Dream, a Financial Institutional and Fintech Coverage professional working with an international bank in Nairobi, Kenya. items.title: Tône/artisanat : 25 mécaniciens des Savanes en formation sur le diagnostic des moteurs
items.description: Dapaong, 19 oct. (ATOP) – Vingt-cinq mécaniciens, membres de la Chambre régionale de métiers (CRM) des Savanes, participent, du 19 au 28 octobre à Dapaong, à une session de formation sur le contrôle d’ensemble, le diagnostic et la mise au point des moteurs diesel et essence. L’initiative est à l’actif de la CRM-Savanes avec l’appui financier du Fonds national d’apprentissage, de formation et de perfectionnement professionnels (FNAFPP) et celui technique du Centre de formation aux métiers de l’industrie (CFMI). Elle vise à renforcer les compétences techniques et pratiques des mécaniciens afin d’améliorer la qualité des prestations de maintenance et de réparation automobile dans la région. Il est question aussi de répondre aux mutations technologiques du secteur automobile, marquées par l’évolution des systèmes de motorisation et l’intégration croissante de dispositifs électroniques. Le but est de réduire les erreurs de diagnostic, les réparations répétitives et le coûts supplémentaires pour les clients. Les bénéficiaires seront outillés sur les principes de fonctionnement des moteurs diesel et essence, le contrôle de leurs différents organes, l’identification des symptômes de panne ainsi que les techniques de diagnostic et de réglage. Les travaux porteront également sur les systèmes d’alimentation, d’injection, d’allumage, de lubrification et de refroidissement, ainsi que sur l’utilisation des instruments de contrôle et de diagnostic automobile. Les participants apprendront à identifier les causes probables des dysfonctionnements mécaniques, électriques et électroniques, à proposer des solutions appropriées et à effectuer les réglages nécessaires à l’optimisation du fonctionnement des moteurs. L’accent sera également mis sur le respect des règles d’hygiène, de sécurité et de protection de l’environnement. A l’issue de la session, ces artisans seront capables de conduire méthodiquement les opérations de contrôle, de diagnostic et de mise au point, afin d’offrir des prestations plus fiables et de renforcer leur professionnalisme ainsi que leur compétitivité. Le secrétaire général de la préfecture de Tône, Dr. Kombate-Sanwogou Soukipiéba a, au nom du gouverneur de la région des Savanes, invité les mécanicien à faire preuve d’assiduité, à partager leur savoir-faire avec leurs apprentis et à collaborer durablement pour renforcer la qualité des services offerts dans la région. Le président de la CRM-Savanes, Damesonou Sambiani, et la conseillère en formation au CFMI, Mme Olou Adara Yesso ont indiqué que face à l’évolution des technologies automobiles, il est indispensable que les mécaniciens actualisent régulièrement leurs connaissances et leurs pratiques. Pour eux, cette formation constitue une opportunité pour renforcer leurs compétences, améliorer la qualité de leurs prestations et accroître la confiance des clients. Le représentant du FNAFPP, Akondi-Ali Ambroise a pour sa part fait remarquer que le renforcement des compétences professionnelles constitue un levier essentiel pour améliorer la productivité, la qualité des services et la compétitivité des artisans. Il a indiqué qu’à travers l’accompagnement de cette formation, le FNAFPP contribue au développement des qualifications techniques et à l’amélioration de l’employabilité dans les métiers de la mécanique automobile. Le président régional des mécaniciens auto des Savanes, Ouro-Akpo Awali participant, a remercié la CRM-Savanes et ses partenaires pour cette initiative qui leur permettra d’actualiser leurs connaissances et de mieux répondre aux exigences du métier. « Nous allons mettre en pratique les acquis de cette formation pour améliorer nos interventions et satisfaire davantage notre clientèle. », a-t-il promis. ATOP/TKA/JK/BA

items.title: Dr Jasaw calls for national agriculture development fund to strengthen climate resilience
items.description: The Wa East MP and Chairman of Parliament’s Food and Agriculture Committee, Dr Godfred Seidu Jasaw has called for the establishment of a National Agriculture Development Fund to strengthen agricultural financing, improve climate resilience and ensure that resources reach farmers and communities exposed to climate-related risks. He said Parliament must play a central role in shaping the institutions through which agricultural financing reaches the economy, stressing the importance of sustainable funding arrangements that support national development priorities. Dr Jasaw made the remarks during discussions at the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, highlighting the role of parliamentary oversight in ensuring that financing commitments translate into practical investments. “I have called for a National Agriculture Development Fund because Parliament must help shape the institutions through which finance reaches the economy,” he said. He noted that the proposed fund could provide a framework for directing resources towards agricultural development while ensuring that Ghana retained control over its investment priorities. Dr Jasaw identified the CVF-V20 as a potential partner in exploring financing options for the fund, emphasising the need to protect national ownership while expanding access to resources. “The CVF-V20 could help Ghana examine financing options for such a fund while retaining national control,” he said. He added that the financing arrangements must ensure that smallholder farmers, women and young people were not excluded from the opportunities created by agricultural investments. “Parliament can provide its legal mandate and ensure that smallholders, women and young people are not crowded out,” he said. Dr Jasaw further stressed that strengthening agricultural financing must go hand in hand with investment in essential infrastructure, including irrigation, feeder roads, storage facilities and local processing capacity. Using examples from Wa East, he explained that irrigation infrastructure alone might not deliver the desired benefits if farmers lacked roads to transport their produce to markets. Similarly, protecting shea trees without developing local processing facilities could leave women undertaking much of the work while the greater economic value was generated elsewhere. “In Wa East, irrigation without a feeder road can still leave a farmer unable to reach the market. A protected shea tree without local processing can leave women doing the hardest work while value is created elsewhere,” he said. He emphasised the need to integrate water, roads, storage, processing, skills and markets to ensure that investments in agriculture deliver meaningful economic benefits to farming communities. The lawmaker also highlighted the importance of preparing for climate-related shocks, particularly drought, which could reduce agricultural production, increase food imports and put pressure on foreign exchange reserves. He called for the relevant finance and agriculture authorities to conduct pre-season stress tests to determine the measures required if agricultural production fell sharply. “Parliament should require the finance and agriculture authorities to conduct a pre-season stress test: if production falls sharply, which inputs and services must continue, who will act and which decisions must already be authorised?” he said. Dr Jasaw said such preparations would help establish clear responsibilities and ensure that essential agricultural inputs and services remained available when climate-related disruptions occurred. He also called on the CVF-V20 to engage parliamentary committees while financing proposals were still being developed, provide options for specific national investments and facilitate the sharing of experiences among climate-vulnerable countries. He said Parliament could support implementation through legislation, budgetary oversight, local evidence and political continuity, helping to identify barriers before they caused delays. Dr Jasaw maintained that agricultural financing should ultimately be assessed by its practical impact on farmers, particularly whether funding arrived within critical planting seasons, infrastructure remained functional after construction and resilience measures generated income for communities facing climate risks. “For my constituents, the test is straightforward. Does finance arrive within the season? Does the investment function after it is built? Does resilience create income where climate risk is being carried?” he asked. He said strengthening agricultural financing institutions and ensuring that investments responded to local needs would be essential to building climate resilience and improving livelihoods across Ghana’s farming communities.

items.title: Une nouvelle étape dans la coopération franco-tunisienne en cancérologie
items.description: Le 15 octobre, au ministère de la Santé tunisien à Tunis, le Pr Norbert VEY, Directeur général de l'Institut Paoli-Calmettes, a officiellement signé un mémorandum d'entente avec l'Institut Salah Azaiez, établissement national de référence en cancérologie en Tunisie. Ce partenariat stratégique vise à renforcer les collaborations entre nos deux institutions dans des domaines majeurs : recherche clinique et translationnelle, innovation médicale, génomique, télémédecine, formation des professionnels de santé, échanges médicaux et paramédicaux, ainsi que le développement de projets scientifiques communs. Cette coopération favorisera le partage d'expertises, la montée en compétences des équipes et l'émergence de nouvelles initiatives au bénéfice des patients des deux rives de la Méditerranée. Par cette signature, l'Institut Paoli-Calmettes réaffirme son engagement en faveur d'une médecine d'excellence, collaborative et ouverte sur l'international, au service du progrès en cancérologie. Nous remercions chaleureusement le Dr Mustapha Ferjani, Ministre tunisien de la Santé, ainsi que l'ensemble des équipes du Ministère de la Santé tunisien et de l'Institut Salah Azaiez pour leur accueil et leur engagement commun au service de la lutte contre le cancer. items.title: Uber wins bid to throw out £200m black cab claims
items.description: Uber has won its bid to throw out claims worth about £340m brought by thousands of London black cab drivers and two former private hire firms. The claimants alleged the ride-hailing company gave Transport for London (TfL) misleading information when it first got a licence to operate in the capital in 2012. But a High Court judge ruled the cases had been brought too late and dismissed them without considering whether the allegations were true. Uber, which denied the claims, said it was pleased the court had thrown them out at the earliest opportunity. About 13,000 drivers were seeking nearly £200m in damages, Reuters reported, while a claim on behalf of Kabbie and Iride, two private hire firms that have since closed, sought about £140m. The lawsuits were filed in 2024, and Uber argued they fell outside the six-year limit for bringing such claims. In a written ruling, Mr Justice Birt said the claimants could have discovered the alleged deception before 2018. RGL Management, which ran the cases for the claimants, said it was very disappointed and was considering its options with the legal team. Since gaining its licence, Uber has taken much of the trade once dominated by black cabs. The company faces a separate case next week, when it challenges HM Revenue and Customs in a tax dispute worth more than £1bn.

items.title: GES releases November 2026 Teachers’ Promotion Examination timetable; Check dates, syllabus and centres nationwide
items.description: The Ghana Education Service has scheduled its November 2026 Teachers’ Promotion Examinations for November 2–4, with candidates in six rank categories expected to sit the examinations according to a designated timetable. The Service has also outlined the examination formats, syllabus, identification requirements and centres across the country. The Ghana Education Service (GES) has outlined the schedule for the November 2026 Teachers’ Promotion Examinations, providing candidates with details of the dates, times, examination formats and designated centres for the exercise. The examinations will take place over three consecutive days, beginning on Monday, November 2, and ending on Wednesday, November 4. Each examination session is scheduled to run from 9.00 am to 11.00 am. Under the timetable, Director I and Director II candidates will write on the first day, while Principal Superintendent and Assistant Director II candidates are scheduled for the second day. Assistant Director I and Deputy Director candidates will sit their examinations on the final day. The announcement provides important guidance for teachers preparing for promotion, particularly regarding the documents they must present, the syllabus they are expected to study and the question formats applicable to their respective ranks. The examination centres listed in the notice include colleges of education, universities and selected senior high schools across several regions of Ghana. GES promotion examination timetable for November 2026 The GES has allocated specific dates to the different categories of candidates to guide preparations for the examinations. The official schedule is as follows: Date Time Rank Monday, November 2, 2026 9.00 am–11.00 am Director I (DI) and Director II (DII) Tuesday, November 3, 2026 9.00 am–11.00 am Assistant Director II (ADII) and Principal Superintendent (PS) Wednesday, November 4, 2026 9.00 am–11.00 am Assistant Director I (ADI) and Deputy Director (DD) All three examination sessions are scheduled for the morning, with candidates expected to observe the date assigned to their respective ranks. Candidates are advised to confirm their individual examination arrangements and ensure they know their designated centres well before the day of the exercise. Candidates to receive SMS notifications One of the key instructions in the examination notice concerns the communication of candidates’ details. According to the GES, SMS messages containing candidates’ Staff IDs, Index Numbers and examination centres will be sent to them ahead of the examinations. The notification system is intended to provide candidates with the information they need to identify their examination venues and confirm their relevant details. Candidates should therefore pay attention to messages received on their registered contact numbers and keep the information available for reference. The Service has also instructed candidates to quote their Staff IDs and Index Numbers on their question papers during the examination. In addition, every candidate is required to present a national identification card bearing their name and photograph at the examination centre. The identification requirement makes it important for candidates to ensure that their documents are available and that their details correspond with the information provided for the examination. Candidates who have concerns about their notifications or personal details should seek clarification through the appropriate GES offices before the examination dates. Where to check names and Index Numbers The GES has identified several offices and locations where candidates can access their names and Index Numbers. These are: GES headquarters; Regional Education Offices; Municipal, Metropolitan and District Education Offices; and Designated examination centres. Candidates who have not received their SMS notifications, or who need to verify their names and Index Numbers, are advised to use these channels to establish their details. Early verification may help candidates resolve discrepancies before the examinations and reduce the risk of last-minute difficulties. The Service has also indicated that other challenges should be channelled through the relevant Municipal, Metropolitan or District Education Offices and Regional Education Offices to the GES headquarters. Examination syllabus: Eight key areas candidates should study The November 2026 Teachers’ Promotion Examinations will cover eight major areas relating to education policy, teaching and learning, school administration and professional practice. The syllabus outlined in the notice includes the following: 1. Knowledge of the Ministry of Education and GES Candidates are expected to prepare for questions relating to the Ministry of Education (MoE) and the Ghana Education Service. A sound understanding of the institutions and their roles in Ghana’s education system will be relevant to this section. 2. School and classroom management This area focuses on the management of schools and classrooms, including the organisation of teaching and learning environments. Candidates should revise the principles and practices associated with effective school and classroom management. 3. Theories of teaching and learning The examination will also assess candidates’ knowledge of theories underpinning teaching and learning. Preparation should include the major concepts and principles that explain how learners acquire knowledge and how teaching can support learning. 4. Curriculum development Curriculum development is another subject area included in the syllabus. Candidates should revise the principles associated with curriculum planning, development and implementation in educational settings. 5. Assessment and evaluation This section concerns assessment and evaluation in education. Candidates should be familiar with the purpose of assessment, the evaluation of learning outcomes and the role these processes play in teaching and learning. 6. Office practices The syllabus includes office practices, an area relevant to professional conduct and administrative responsibilities within educational institutions and offices. 7. Contemporary national and international issues Candidates will also be examined on contemporary issues at both national and international levels. Keeping abreast of significant developments and understanding their potential relevance to education may therefore form part of candidates’ preparations. 8. Educational administration and management The final listed area is educational administration and management. This subject is particularly relevant to the leadership and supervisory responsibilities associated with higher professional ranks within the education service. Taken together, the eight topics cover both teaching-related knowledge and the administrative responsibilities that underpin the management of educational institutions. Candidates are encouraged to use the published syllabus as a guide for organising their revision and to avoid concentrating exclusively on one subject area. Question formats differ according to candidates’ ranks The GES has also outlined the number and types of questions candidates should expect, with the format varying according to rank. Understanding these differences will help candidates tailor their revision and practise the relevant question types. Principal Superintendent, Assistant Director II and Assistant Director I Candidates in the Principal Superintendent, Assistant Director II and Assistant Director I categories will answer 75 multiple-choice or true/false questions . Candidates in these categories should prepare to identify correct answers, distinguish between accurate and inaccurate statements, and revise the concepts covered by the examination syllabus. Deputy Director Deputy Director candidates will answer 60 multiple-choice or true/false questions, plus 15 fill-in questions. This format requires preparation for both objective questions and questions that require candidates to supply missing information. Candidates should therefore revise key terminology, concepts and relevant factual information alongside practising multiple-choice and true/false questions. Director I and Director II Candidates sitting the Director I and Director II examinations will answer 40 multiple-choice questions and 60 short-answer or fill-in-the-blank questions. The format places considerable emphasis on short-answer and completion questions in addition to multiple-choice questions. Candidates should allocate adequate time to recalling relevant information and expressing answers accurately and concisely. The question formats specified in the notice underline the importance of preparing according to the requirements of each rank rather than relying on a single revision approach. Examination centres across Ghana The GES has listed examination centres across the Ahafo, Ashanti, Bono, Bono East, Central, Eastern, Greater Accra, Northern, North East, Savannah, Upper East, Upper West, Oti, Volta, Western and Western North areas. The centres include colleges of education, universities and senior high schools. The notice also identifies the ranks scheduled at individual venues. Candidates should therefore confirm both their assigned centre and the ranks accommodated at that location, rather than assuming that every centre will host every category. The following is a regional breakdown of the centres listed in the supplied examination information. Ahafo Region The designated centre listed for the Ahafo Region is: St Joseph’s College of Education, Bechem: Principal Superintendent (PS), Assistant Director II (ADII), Assistant Director I (ADI) and Deputy Director (DD). Ashanti Region The Ashanti Region has eight listed examination centres: Agogo College of Education, Akim Agogo — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Agona SDA College of Education, Agona-Mampong — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Akrokerri College of Education, Akrokerri — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Offinso College of Education, Offinso — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. St Monica’s College of Education, Mampong — ADII and ADI. St Louis College of Education, Kumasi — PS and ADI. University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development (USTED), KSI — ADII and DD. Wesley College of Education, Kumasi — DI, DII, PS, ADII and ADI. Candidates in the Ashanti Region should pay particular attention to the ranks listed against their intended centres, as the range of ranks differs between institutions. Bono Region Four examination centres are listed for the Bono Region: Al-Farouq College of Education, Wenchi — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Berekum College of Education, Berekum — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. St Ambrose College of Education, Dormaa — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Sunyani Technical University — DI, DII, PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Sunyani Technical University is listed for all six ranks covered by the timetable. Bono East Region The listed examination centres in the Bono East Region are: Atebubu College of Education, Atebubu — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. University of Education, Winneba, CODeL Study Centre, Techiman — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Candidates should confirm the specific venue assigned to them before travelling for the examination. Central Region Four centres are listed in the Central Region: Foso College of Education, Assin Foso — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. University of Education, Winneba, North Campus, Winneba — ADII and DD. University of Education, Winneba, South Campus, Winneba — PS and ADI. University of Cape Coast (NLT), Cape Coast — DI, DII, PS, ADII, ADI and DD. The University of Cape Coast venue is listed for all six ranks, while the two University of Education, Winneba campuses have different rank allocations. Eastern Region The Eastern Region has seven listed examination centres: Abetifi College of Education — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Kibi College of Education, Kibi — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Methodist College of Education, Akim Oda — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Mt Mary College of Education, Somanya — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Presbyterian College of Education (PCE), Akropong — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Presbyterian Women’s College of Education (PWCE), Aburi — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Seventh Day Adventists’ College of Education, Koforidua — DI, DII, PS, ADII, ADI and DD. The region’s listed centres cover a range of ranks, with the Seventh Day Adventists’ College of Education in Koforidua accommodating all six categories according to the supplied information. Greater Accra Region Four centres have been listed for the Greater Accra Region: Accra College of Education — DI, DII, PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Presbyterian Boys Senior High School, Accra — ADII, ADI and DD. Ada College of Education — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Chemu Senior High School, Tema — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Accra College of Education is listed for all six ranks, while the other centres have more specific allocations. Candidates in Greater Accra should check their SMS notifications carefully to establish which of the listed institutions has been assigned to them. Northern, North East, Savannah and Upper West areas The supplied notice groups the following centres under the Northern, North East, Savannah and Upper West areas: University for Development Studies (UDS), Tamale — DI, DII, PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Bimbilla College of Education — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Gambaga College of Education — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. NJA College of Education, Wa — DII, PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Tumu College of Education — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Candidates in these areas should use their individual notifications to confirm the precise examination venue and avoid relying solely on the regional grouping in a summary of the notice. Upper East Region Two centres are listed for the Upper East Region: Gbewaa College of Education, Pusiga — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. St John Bosco’s College of Education, Navrongo — DII, PS, ADII, ADI and DD. The ranks accommodated at the two institutions differ, making it important for candidates to confirm their designated centre. Oti Region The Oti Region has two listed examination centres: Dambai College of Education — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Jasikan College of Education — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Both centres are listed for Principal Superintendent, Assistant Director II, Assistant Director I and Deputy Director candidates. Volta Region Four centres are listed in the Volta Region: Holy Spirit College of Education, Ho — PS and ADI. Ho Technical University, Ho — DI, DII, ADII, ADI and DD. St Teresa’s College of Education, Hohoe — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Akatsi College of Education — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Candidates should note that the rank allocations vary across the four venues. Western Region The Western Region has three listed centres: Holy Child College of Education, Takoradi — DI, DII, ADII and ADI. Fijai Senior High School, Takoradi — ADII and ADI. University of Mines and Technology (UMaT), Tarkwa — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. The different allocations mean that candidates should not select a centre based solely on proximity. Their individual examination notifications should guide them. Western North Region Two examination centres are listed for the Western North Region: Wiawso College of Education — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Enchi College of Education — PS, ADII, ADI and DD. Both institutions are listed for Principal Superintendent, Assistant Director II, Assistant Director I and Deputy Director candidates. Special examination arrangements for candidates with additional needs The GES has identified three dedicated examination centres for candidates with special needs requiring accommodation, particularly those who are visually challenged. The designated centres are: Wesley College of Education, Kumasi; Presbyterian College of Education, Akropong; and NJA College of Education, Wa. Candidates who require special assistance have been advised to make all necessary contacts and arrangements before the examination day. This instruction is particularly important for candidates who may need specific accommodation to participate effectively in the examination. Candidates requiring assistance should communicate their needs early enough for the necessary arrangements to be considered. What candidates should do before examination day With the first examination scheduled for Monday, 2 November 2026, candidates should use the period before the exercise to complete their revision and verify their administrative arrangements. The following steps are recommended: Confirm your examination date. Check the timetable against your current rank to establish the correct day for your examination. Look out for your SMS notification. The message is expected to contain your Staff ID, Index Number and examination centre. Verify your personal details. Candidates can check their names and Index Numbers at the GES headquarters, Regional Education Offices, Municipal, Metropolitan and District Education Offices, and designated examination centres. Prepare your identification card. A national identification card bearing your name and photograph must be presented at the examination centre. Revise all eight syllabus areas. Candidates should cover the topics identified in the notice, including knowledge of MoE and GES, school management, curriculum development, assessment and educational administration. Practise your rank-specific question format. The number and types of questions differ by rank, so candidates should structure their preparation accordingly. Arrange special assistance in advance. Candidates who require accommodations should contact the appropriate authorities before their scheduled examination date. Raise any concerns through the appropriate channels. Other challenges should be referred through the relevant Municipal, Metropolitan or District Education Offices and Regional Education Offices to the GES headquarters. These preparations can help candidates approach the examination with a clearer understanding of the requirements and reduce avoidable administrative difficulties. What the announcement means for teachers seeking promotion The November 2026 examination schedule provides a framework for candidates to organise their final preparations ahead of the promotion exercise. The published syllabus spans educational policy, classroom practice, curriculum development, assessment, office procedures and educational leadership. These subjects are relevant to the professional responsibilities associated with teaching, supervision and school administration. The different question formats also mean that candidates need to understand the requirements of the examination for their respective ranks. For those seeking promotion, careful revision and compliance with the GES instructions will be important aspects of their preparation. Candidates should therefore rely on further official communication from the GES for information about results and subsequent administrative processes.

items.title: Mamponghene warns against galamsey, destructive sand winning at Akrofonso
items.description: The Paramount Chief of Asante Mampong, Daasebre Osei Bonsu III, has cautioned against illegal mining and improper sand winning at Mampong Akrofonso, warning that the community’s lands and water bodies must be protected for sustainable development. He said the lands around Mampong Akrofonso should be used for productive investments that create jobs and improve livelihoods, rather than activities that degrade the environment and threaten the community’s water resources. Daasebre Osei Bonsu III gave the warning during a three-day visit to Mampong Akrofonso over the weekend to perform traditional rites required of every Asante Mampong paramount chief. The visit forms part of a long-standing tradition in which every Omanhene of Asante Mampong must return to the ancestral town to perform spiritual rituals to affirm and consolidate his kingship. Following his confirmation as Mamponghene, as directed by the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, Daasebre Osei Bonsu III travelled to the town to fulfil the customary obligation. Addressing the people, the Mamponghene said he was committed to reorganising the community and advancing the welfare of its residents, particularly the youth. He assured them that Mampong Akrofonso would not be left out of development initiatives in Asante Mampong. He also entrusted the affairs of the community to the Mampong Akrofonsohene, Nana Baffour Gyimah Ankoana, urging him to identify suitable land for the establishment of handicraft enterprises to provide employment opportunities for young people. Daasebre Osei Bonsu III emphasised that protecting the environment must be central to the community’s development agenda, stressing the need to safeguard water bodies from pollution and preserve them for future generations. The Mampong Akrofonsohene, Nana Baffour Gyimah Ankoana, said the visit demonstrated the paramount chief’s commitment to fulfilling the traditional responsibilities required to strengthen his reign. He explained that Mampong Akrofonso had available land that could be allocated to credible investors interested in establishing schools, hospitals, police stations and factories. According to him, such investments would expand economic opportunities, create jobs and support the development of the community. Nana Baffour Gyimah Ankoana maintained that the youth of Mampong Akrofonso had the potential to contribute meaningfully to development if given the necessary opportunities and support. He appealed to Daasebre Osei Bonsu III to provide guidance and assistance as he carried out his responsibilities as chief. The call for responsible land use and environmental protection reinforces the need for communities to balance economic development with the preservation of natural resources, particularly water bodies that sustain livelihoods and public health.

items.title: Obuasi SHTS has become a crime scene – Salaga South MP
items.description: Member of Parliament for Salaga South and Vice-Chairperson of Parliament’s Gender, Children and Social Welfare Committee, Zuwera Mohammed Ibrahimah, has described Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) as a “big crime scene” following allegations of sexual abuse involving the school’s headteacher. Her comments come after the number of students who have come forward with allegations of sexual abuse involving the suspended headmaster of Obuasi SHTS has risen from 16 to 19 following the airing of JoyNews Investigative Journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni’s latest documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow. “From this documentary, mainly, the school is a big crime scene. The school is not a place where mothers want their daughters to go. The school is not a place where we can sleep knowing that our children are being taken care of,” she said. Speaking on JoyNews ‘ The Pulse on Monday, October 19, she condemned the failure of authorities and other stakeholders to act decisively on reports of abuse, saying their inaction had undermined efforts to secure justice for the affected girls. “Society conspired to deny these girls justice and to enable the predatory work of this headteacher,” she added. The MP also questioned why the headteacher had not been arrested, noting that his suspension by the Ghana Education Service appeared to be the only action taken against him. Madam Ibrahimah expressed concern that the headteacher had allegedly been able to return to his community while the legal process had yet to take its course. The MP further criticised education officials and other authorities who reportedly received petitions from the girls but failed to take the necessary action. She, however, commended the students for their courage in seeking justice, saying they had submitted petitions to several authorities, including education directors and local government officials. “I celebrate their courage and I celebrate them,” she said. The MP said the allegations should prompt a more critical examination of the school environment and the responsibility of authorities to protect children entrusted to their care.

items.title: Obuasi SHTS abuse: PTA association calls for action against alleged perpetrators
items.description: The General Secretary of the National Council of Parent-Teacher Associations, Gapson Kofi Raphael, has called for action against persons implicated in the alleged sexual abuse of students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) and those suspected of covering up the incidents. He says the allegations must be thoroughly investigated and anyone found to have condoned or concealed criminal conduct held accountable. Speaking on JoyNews ‘ The Pulse on Monday, October 19, Mr Raphael expressed disappointment in the handling of the matter by school authorities and the Ghana Education Service (GES), questioning the effectiveness of the committee established to investigate the allegations. He added that parents must have confidence that their children are safe while under the care of school administrators and teachers. “It is clear from the information we have gathered from within the school that they were trying to whitewash the case and sweep the actual issues under the carpet. We should be able to deal decisively with those who condone or cover up crime. This is criminal conduct, and we must allow the law to deal with it.” He also criticised the school’s Parent-Teacher Association (PTA) leadership for failing to champion the concerns of affected students and their parents. According to him, the PTA chairman and secretary should have led efforts to ensure the complaints were addressed rather than allowing the matter to be overlooked. Mr Raphael further faulted the GES Director-General and his team for waiting until the Education Minister issued a statement before taking disciplinary action against the headteacher, who has since been suspended. He insisted that a person’s political influence, cultural background or social standing must not prevent victims from accessing justice. “No amount of influence, whether political, whether cultural, whether social standing of an individual, should be allowed to take precedence over the welfare of a child who is in the custody of that person,” he said. His comments follow a JoyNews investigative documentary by Manasseh Azure Awuni detailing allegations of sexual abuse involving students at the school and raising questions about how complaints were handled by school authorities and other stakeholders.

items.title: Jeneral Ntatia recalls how his father’s death changed his life
items.description: Comedian Jeneral Ntatia has opened up about the painful loss of his father, revealing how the experience transformed his life and thrust him into the difficult reality of carrying family responsibilities as the firstborn son. The comedian became emotional as he recounted the events surrounding his father’s death, describing how a day that began with reassurance that everything would be fine ended with news that changed his life forever. Speaking in an interview on Joy Prime with Nikki Samonas , Ntatia disclosed that he was undertaking his national service when his mother called one morning to inform him that his father was unwell. His father later took the phone and assured him there was no cause for alarm, explaining that his mother was simply worried about his condition. However, a second call later in the afternoon brought a more worrying update: his father was in critical condition, and he needed to rush home to Osino. “So I was going to Osino and then when I got to Suhum, a friend of his called me and it was like, at first they said I should come to the hospital, Chebi Hospital. And then on the way they called me that I should come home to Osino because they’ve done everything. They’ve left him there, so I should come home and then tomorrow morning we’ll go and visit him”. It was only after arriving home that the devastating truth began to emerge. For Ntatia, that was the moment the reality of his loss finally sank in. He had imagined losing a loved one might happen someday, but nothing could have prepared him for the moment it became his own reality. As the firstborn son, his grief came with an overwhelming list of responsibilities. He had to think about how to inform his grandmother, how to break the news to his siblings and how to support his mother, who was living on someone else’s land in Osino, far from their roots in Adansi Fomena. Despite the shock, Ntatia believes his father had, in some ways, prepared him for the responsibility that lay ahead. During his later years, his father repeatedly reminded him that he was the captain of the ship and would eventually have to take charge and continue the journey. “A lot of things are running through my head. But then I think my dad did an ) amazing job. In his latter days, he kept telling me that I’m the captain of the ship and then he’s going to leave the battle for me to continue so I should be ready for anything.” Although his father had been unwell, the family had remained hopeful that he would recover. His condition had not appeared to them to be something that would take his life, making the loss even harder to accept. Born Prince Kwame Amoabeng, the death of his father was more than just a heartbreaking family loss; it was a turning point that forced him to confront adulthood. His account offers a glimpse into the private struggles behind the laughter audiences’ associate with the comedian.

items.title: Ghana Publishing Company launches online bookshop for Acts of Parliament, Constitution
items.description: Ghanaians can now order Acts of Parliament, copies of the Constitution and other official publications online and have them delivered to their locations without travelling to Accra. The service follows the introduction of an online bookshop by the Ghana Publishing Company Limited (GPCL) to improve public access to government publications. Speaking at a press conference in Accra on Monday, October 19, 2026, GPCL Managing Director, Nana Kwasi Boatey, Esq., said the initiative was designed to address the difficulties people face in obtaining copies of Ghana’s laws. He explained that people living outside Accra often had to travel long distances to purchase Acts of Parliament and other publications, sometimes spending more on transportation than on the documents themselves. According to him, GPCL’s limited physical presence across the country had also created opportunities for the unauthorised printing and sale of Acts of Parliament. The online bookshop is expected to make it easier for individuals and institutions to obtain genuine copies directly from the state-owned publishing company. Under the system, customers can visit GPCL’s website, select the publications they need, place their orders and have the items delivered to their preferred locations. The service covers publications sold at GPCL’s Business Centre, including Acts of Parliament and copies of the Constitution. Mr Boatey said the initiative was partly in response to requests from members of the public for a more convenient way to access government publications. He added that the company was also working to improve electronic access to its publications. The online bookshop is expected to reduce the time and transportation costs associated with obtaining official documents, particularly for people living outside the national capital. The initiative forms part of GPCL’s efforts to use technology to expand access to its services across the country.

items.title: Mali : Les FAMa frappent deux bases terroristes à Ménaka et Douentza
items.description: Dans le cadre de l'opération Dougoukoloko, les Forces armées maliennes (FAMa), appuyées par leurs partenaires, ont mené des frappes de précision contre deux positions de groupes armés terroristes. Les opérations ont eu lieu les samedi 17 et dimanche 18 octobre 2026, respectivement au sud-ouest de Ménaka et de Douentza. L'information a été rendue publique ce lundi 19 octobre 2026 dans un communiqué émanant de l'État-major général des armées. Les Forces armées maliennes poursuivent la traque des terroristes sur l'ensemble du territoire. Selon le communiqué de l'État-major général, l'exploitation de renseignements précis a permis, le samedi 17 octobre 2026, de localiser une importante base abritant plusieurs éléments terroristes ainsi que du matériel de guerre et de logistique, à 65 km au sud-ouest de la ville de Ménaka. Après confirmation des renseignements recueillis et appréciation de la situation, le site a été ciblé et frappé avec succès. Le lendemain, dimanche 18 octobre 2026, un point de concentration de groupes armés terroristes disposant de matériel de guerre et de motocyclettes a été localisé à 35 km au sud-ouest de la ville de Douentza. Après une phase d'observation et d'analyse, la position a fait l'objet de plusieurs frappes de précision. D'après le communiqué, les opérations de surveillance et de reconnaissance se poursuivent dans les secteurs concernés. Elles visent à évaluer avec précision les effets des actions menées, à en établir un bilan consolidé et à rechercher puis neutraliser toute menace résiduelle. L'État-major général des armées réaffirme la détermination des Forces armées maliennes à poursuivre les opérations de sécurisation sur l'ensemble du territoire national avec rigueur, professionnalisme et engagement. Il invite les populations à maintenir leur soutien et leur confiance aux forces engagées. Lire aussi : Mali : Les FAMa reprennent le contrôle total d’Anéfis Minute.bf

items.title: Ghana signs $28bn investment deal with Consortium for Phase 2, Petroleum Hub Project
items.description: The Petroleum Hub Development Corporation has signed a 28-billion-dollar investment agreement with an international investment consortium to build Phase 2 of the Petroleum Hub Project at Jomoro in the Western Region, a major boost to the government’s 24-Hour Economy programme. The project, which is expected to commence in the first quarter of 2027, will be completed in 2031. Speaking at the signing ceremony, Chief Executive of the Petroleum Hub Development Corporation, Dr. Toni Aubynn, said the project will reduce dependence on imported fuel, save foreign exchange, and create jobs operating round-the-clock. “Todays agreement sends a strong signal to the international investment community. it demonstrates that Ghana remains the trusted destination for long-term investments underpinned by political stability. We welcome investors who share our vision of creating value, generating employment and advancing sustainable industrial development”. Representative of the Investment Consortium, Bou-ba-car Belco Bah, pledged to collaborate with the Petroleum Hub Development Corporation to ensure the project is executed within the stipulated time frame. “We are committed to responsible development in accordance with Ghanaian laws and regulations and appropriate international standards. We also recognize the importance of technology transfer, local capacity building and development of skills of Ghanaian professionals. Industrial progress must be measured by work and safety, community protection and long-term sustainability”. On his part, the Minister of Energy and Green Transition, Dr. John Jinapor, assured PHDC of government’s resolve to transform Ghana’s energy sector. “I have asked for a meeting so that we can discuss what we can do to ensure that we can achieve this objective, and as a minister I have to give you all the support that I can, shepherd it, and ensure we meet our side of the bargain so that we can create this enabling environment for you to achieve this objective. You have my full support”. Meanwhile, the Petroleum Hub Project, first proposed in 2020 under the Petroleum Hub Development Corporation Act, is expected to create over 700,000 direct and indirect jobs when all phases are completed.

items.title: McCullum wary of Pakistan’s home advantage as England prepare for tri-series test
items.description: England head coach Brendon McCullum has warned his side they will need to adapt quickly to subcontinent conditions to compete against Pakistan and Sri Lanka, as the visitors prepare to face the hosts in the second match of the One-day International tri-series at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Tuesday. McCullum acknowledged Pakistan’s familiarity with home conditions and the challenge of winning away from home, but said England were eager to test themselves against two strong opponents in a competition that will also serve as preparation for next year’s 50-over World Cup. “Pakistan’s a very strong side,” McCullum said during a media talk on Monday. “When you come to this part of the world, you have to do things differently. Playing subcontinent teams in subcontinent conditions has its own challenges, but that’s something we’re looking forward to.” England arrive with momentum after three consecutive ODI series victories in 2026, but the prospect of facing Pakistan on their home ground presents a different examination. The visitors will also have to contend with Sri Lanka, with the top two sides from the double round-robin stage qualifying for the Oct 31 final in Lahore. McCullum said England wanted to be competitive against any opposition and in all conditions, rather than rely on a fixed approach. “We don’t have any kind of binary process of how we want to go about playing,” he said. “We want to just make sure that we play what’s in front of us, adapt as quick as we can, and hopefully try and play the best cricket we can to give ourselves a chance.” Pakistan, meanwhile, enter Tuesday’s fixture after beginning their campaign with a 37-run victory over Sri Lanka on Sunday. A match-winning century from Salman Ali Agha helped the hosts post 305 before their pace attack bowled Sri Lanka out for 268, giving captain Shaheen Shah Afridi’s side an encouraging start to the tournament. Salman’s unbeaten 107 off 90 balls was particularly significant after a difficult period in his international career. Having been left out of Pakistan’s T20 and Test sides, the middle-order batter returned to domestic cricket, where substantial first-class scores helped him regain form ahead of his comeback. Speaking after the Sri Lanka match, Salman called for greater recognition of performances in domestic cricket, saying: “I feel that we don’t give enough respect to our domestic cricket.” He argued that scoring runs at that level was not as straightforward as some critics suggested, adding that players had to work hard to earn their runs. His own return offered a timely illustration of how domestic cricket can help players rebuild confidence and address technical shortcomings before returning to the international stage. Salman’s innings also underlined the importance of Pakistan’s middle order against an England attack that includes experienced campaigners and several emerging players. His ability to anchor an innings while scoring at a healthy rate could prove valuable if Pakistan lose early wickets against England’s seamers. The hosts will also look to their fast bowlers to build on Sunday’s performance. Shaheen, Naseem Shah, Haris Rauf and Faheem Ashraf shared all 10 Sri Lankan wickets, demonstrating the depth of Pakistan’s pace resources. However, Sri Lanka’s fifth-wicket partnership between Janith Liyanage and Pavan Rathnayake showed that Pakistan’s attack can be challenged if batters settle in. England, for their part, have assembled a squad combining established names with players seeking to establish themselves in the ODI side. Former captain Joe Root brings experience and stability, while Harry Brook, who leads the team in white-ball cricket, will be central to their batting plans. Will Jacks offers an additional option with both bat and ball, while leg-spinner Adil Rashid and all-rounder Sam Curran have returned to the squad after injuries. England will, however, be without Jos Buttler, who is recovering from a hamstring injury, while fast bowler Jofra Archer has been rested to manage his workload. The absence of two prominent players places added responsibility on the available squad to deliver in unfamiliar conditions. McCullum said the team understood the advantage Pakistan enjoyed at home but viewed the challenge as an opportunity to improve their adaptability. He also welcomed the chance to play in a tri-series, describing the format as a distinctive test because teams must adjust to different opponents in quick succession. “It’s a real opportunity in front of us,” he said, adding that England respected the strength of both Pakistan and Sri Lanka and would need to be at their best to reach the final. Tuesday’s match is the first of two meetings between Pakistan and England in the league stage. The sides will meet again in Lahore on Oct 25, while England face Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi on Thursday. With the final scheduled for Lahore on Oct 31, a strong start could prove decisive in the race for qualification.

items.title: CRIEF : Tommy Mathew, de nationalités sierra-léonaise et américaine, s’évade de l’hôpital sino-guinéen, le Parquet spécial annonce des poursuites
items.description: Le parquet spécial près la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF) a annoncé, ce lundi 19 octobre 2026, la fuite de Tommy Mathew, de double nationalité sierra-léonaise et américaine, alors qu’il était hospitalisé sous surveillance à l’hôpital de l’amitié sino-guinéen. Le parquet annonce des poursuites pour des faits présumés de complicité d’évasion et promet de tout mettre en œuvre pour retrouver le fugitif. Nouvelle affaire à la CRIEF. Tommy Mathew, de nationalités sierra-léonaise et américaine, a pris la fuite alors qu’il faisait l’objet d’une ordonnance de placement en milieu hospitalier, selon un communiqué du parquet spécial publié ce lundi 19 octobre 2026. « Le parquet spécial près la Cour de Répression des Infractions Economiques et Financières (CRIEF), a été informé par le Directeur national de l’administration pénitentiaire, de la fuite de Monsieur Tommy MATHEW, de double-nationalité Léonaise et Américaine à l’hôpital de l’amitié Sino-guinéen », indique le communiqué. signé du Service de communication institutionnelle du parquet spécial. D’après le parquet spécial, Tommy Mathew était hospitalisé en vertu de l’ordonnance n° 265/CI/CRIEF/2026 du 30 septembre 2026, rendue par la chambre de l’instruction de la CRIEF. Cette décision était assortie d’une surveillance dont la mise en œuvre relevait notamment du directeur national de l’administration pénitentiaire et de la réinsertion, du régisseur de la maison d’arrêt et de correction de Coyah ainsi que des gardes pénitentiaires désignés. Des poursuites annoncées pour complicité d’évasion Face à cette situation, le parquet spécial annonce des démarches judiciaires pour établir les responsabilités liées à cette fuite. « Face à cette situation, le parquet spécial, en attendant de situer les différentes responsabilités, informe l’opinion de la saisine du parquet compétent pour des faits présumés de complicité d’évasion », précise le communiqué. Le parquet spécial assure également qu’il entend rechercher activement le fugitif afin qu’il réponde des faits qui lui sont reprochés. « Le parquet spécial […] rassure qu’il fera tout ce qui est en son pouvoir pour rechercher le fugitif afin qu’il réponde des faits d’atteinte grave à la santé publique », ajoute le document. Le parquet appelle à se référer à ses canaux officiels Afin d’éviter la circulation d’informations incomplètes, le parquet spécial invite le public à privilégier ses canaux de communication officiels. « Pour éviter des informations parcellaires, le parquet spécial invite toutes personnes ayant intérêt à se référer uniquement aux informations relayées à travers nos canaux de communication officiels », souligne le communiqué. Ousmane CAMARA L’article CRIEF : Tommy Mathew, de nationalités sierra-léonaise et américaine, s’évade de l’hôpital sino-guinéen, le Parquet spécial annonce des poursuites est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Sénégal : lancement du Comité de gouvernance du numérique pour accompagner la transformation digitale du pays
items.description: Un pas decisif vient d'etre franchi, selon le gouvernement senegalais le 18 octobre, dans la structuration de son ecosysteme digital avec l'installation officielle du Comite de gouvernance du numerique (GouvNum) par le Premier ministre Ahmadou Al Aminou Mohamed Lo, qui a place l'evenement dans la continuite du « New deal technologique, qui est la declinaison sectorielle de l'agenda national de transition 2050 ». Cette nouvelle structure, placee sous l'autorite du chef du gouvernement, « doit garantir la conformite des projets a l'architecture commune, consolider et prioriser les investissements, prevenir les redondances, maîtriser les coûts sur les cycles de vie des systemes et veiller aux exigences de securite, d'interoperabilite et de protection des donnees », a-t-il explique. La nouvelle instance de gouvernance est composee de ministeres sectoriels et de structures parapubliques. Elle est percue par le gouvernement senegalais comme un outil permettant de materialiser l'ambition d'une societe numerique a l'horizon 2034. Les benefices de l'ambition numerique Faisant du numerique un moteur de transformation economique, de modernisation de l'etat et d'amelioration des conditions de vie, le gouvernement senegalais s'est fixe les objectifs de porter la contribution du numerique au produit interieur brut (PIB) a 15 %, de creer 150 000 emplois directs, de numeriser 90 % des procedures administratives, de garantir un taux de connectivite de 90 % sur le territoire et de doter 90 % des citoyens d'une identite numerique d'ici 2034. Ces elements sont indiques dans un communique de la Primature du Senegal, publie sur la page officielle du ministere senegalais des Telecommunications et du Numerique. La meme source a aussi salue les contributions des partenaires de l'operationalisation du Comite de gouvernance du numerique a travers le projet « Goin'Digital » finance par l'Union europeenne au Senegal, la Cooperation allemande et la France.
